alert_actions.conf: Specification file is the wrong version. The shipped splunk-spec-files/alert_actions.conf.spec declares "# Version 10.0.0" and is 623 lines; the 10.4.2 instance ships "# Version 10.4.2" at 680 lines (podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer head -1 /opt/splunk/etc/system/README/alert_actions.conf.spec). Every line citation in internal_dev/verify2/alert_actions.json points into the 10.0.0 file and is off against 10.4.2: [email] 157 vs 176, mailserver 276 vs 312, sslVersions 428 vs 482, sslVerifyServerCert 441 vs 496, [webhook] 599 vs 656, enable_allowlist 605 vs 662, allowlist.<name> 617 vs 674. Only command (87) coincides.

sslVersions vocabulary is materially different between the two. Shipped 10.0.0 spec: "sslVersions = <string>", "The versions available are \"ssl3\", \"tls1.0\", \"tls1.1\", and \"tls1.2\"", plus a FIPS note about ssl3. Vendor 10.4.2 spec and the published 10.4 reference: "sslVersions = <comma-separated list>", "The versions available are \"tls1.0\", \"tls1.1\", \"tls1.2\", and \"tls1.3\"", "SSL versions 2 and 3 are always disabled", and a new caution that tls1.0/tls1.1 do not work under Python 3.9. The criterion's claim that "the vocabulary and the tls1.2 value match" was drawn from a specification that does not know TLS 1.3 exists.

No vendor source states the sslVersions default. Both spec versions and help.splunk.com defer to "$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf file for the current default". The actual 10.4.2 default is "tls1.2, tls1.3". A criterion written from the documentation alone cannot know this; only the instance shows it, and it is what makes the equals tls1.2 condition wrong.

enable_allowlist default is stated inconsistently by two vendor files inside the same 10.4.2 install. /opt/splunk/etc/system/README/alert_actions.conf.spec says plainly "Default: false". /opt/splunk/etc/apps/alert_webhook/README/alert_actions.conf.spec says "Default (for Splunk Cloud Platform): true" and "Default (for all other Splunk products including Splunk Enterprise): false". The app spec also contradicts itself: "A value of \"true\" means that the webhook allowlist is turned on, and that the Splunk platform lets the webhook action query against any endpoint." The published 10.4 "Configure webhook allow list" page resolves the intent: enabling it without entries authorizes any URL.

disabled is honored for alert actions but documented nowhere. The hardening configuration in /opt/splunk/etc/system/local/alert_actions.conf sets "[email] disabled = 1", btool resolves it, and splunk_secure_gateway ships "disabled = 0" for its own action. The key appears in neither the 10.0.0 nor the 10.4.2 spec, nor on the published 10.4 reference page. splunk btool check returns zero lines and exit 0 and does not flag it, so btool check cannot be used to validate key names in this file.

The shipped configuration contradicts eight of the conditions it is assessed against. On the instance [email] has disabled = 1 and allowedDomainList = localhost. Per the 10.4.2 spec, a comma-separated allowedDomainList allows only the named domains and "Splunk software automatically removes the address from the recipient list" for anything else. So the email action is switched off and restricted to the localhost domain, meaning the mailserver, from and stanza-presence conditions can all be satisfied while no notification can leave the host.
Minor: the 10.4.2 system spec points readers to "the alert-actions.conf.spec file in the alert_webhook app". The file is named alert_actions.conf.spec, with an underscore.
authentication.conf: VERSION MISMATCH, the structural defect of this file. The shipped specification copy in splunk-spec-files/authentication.conf.spec is headed '#   Version 10.0.0' and is 1729 lines. The specification the vendor ships inside the 10.4.2 instance (etc/system/README/authentication.conf.spec) is headed '#   Version 10.4.2' and is 2126 lines. Every line-number citation in every rationale in this file points into the 10.0.0 copy: lockoutUsers is cited at :514 but is at :535 in 10.4.2; enablePasswordHistory cited at :554 is at :575; enableMfaAuthRest cited at :1568 is at :1685; passwordHashAlgorithm cited at :58 is at :50. I extracted all 20 settings from both files and compared declarations, ranges and defaults: the SUBSTANCE is identical in every case, so no operand is wrong because of this. Only the citations are unusable for 10.4.2.

minPasswordLength range. The vendor password-policy page states 'Splunk Enterprise supports values between 1 and 256 characters.' The shipped specification states only '<positive integer>', 'Values less than 1 are ignored.', 'Default: 8' and declares NO maximum. The 10.4 configuration reference also declares no maximum. The documented 256 ceiling exists in no specification file, so a specification-driven criterion cannot know it. The operand 15 is inside the range either way.

PASSWORD POLICY APPLICABILITY, the most consequential disagreement. The vendor password-policy page states plainly: 'Password policies do not apply when you configure the instance to use the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) or Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) authentication schemes', and that the policy 'works with the native authentication scheme for Splunk Enterprise only.' The shipped specification never says this. It says only '[splunk_auth] * Settings for Splunk's internal authentication system.' The consequence crosses conditions inside this one file: SRG-APP-000148-AU-002270 requires [authentication] authType to be LDAP or SAML, while nine conditions across SRG-APP-000164-AU-002480, SRG-APP-000174-AU-002570, SRG-APP-000516-WSR-000079, SRG-APP-000845-AU-000320, SRG-APP-000845-WSR-000220, SRG-APP-000860-AU-000350, SRG-APP-000860-WSR-000250 and SRG-APP-000870-WSR-000270 require [splunk_auth] password settings. Per the vendor, remediating the first makes the other nine inert for every federated user. Nothing in the specification would reveal this, and no amount of re-reading the specification would have caught it. The condition set needs an applicability note: the [splunk_auth] conditions govern native accounts only, and composition, expiration and history for federated users belong in external_dependencies against the identity provider.

passwordHashAlgorithm rounds floor. Both the vendor reference and the shipped specification state 'The number of rounds must be at least 1000', but the declared vocabulary line 'passwordHashAlgorithm = [SHA512-crypt|SHA256-crypt|SHA512-crypt-<num_rounds>|SHA256-crypt-<num_rounds>|MD5-crypt]' imposes no floor on <num_rounds>. A criterion built from the vocabulary line alone, as SRG-APP-000429-WSR-000113's regex ^SHA512-crypt(-[0-9]+)?$ was, admits SHA512-crypt-1.

passwordHashAlgorithm scope. Both the vendor reference and the shipped specification state 'This setting only affects new password settings (either when a user is added or a user's password is changed). Existing passwords work but retain their previous hashing algorithm.' No rationale in this file reflects it, so five conditions treat the setting as though it re-hashes stored credentials on being set. It does not.

enableMfaAuthRest stanza notation. The shipped specification and the 10.4 vendor reference BOTH present the stanza as the placeholder '[<duo-externalTwoFactorAuthSettings-key>]', with the bullet '<duo-externalTwoFactorAuthSettings-key> must be the value listed in the externalTwoFactorAuthSettings setting, specified in the [authentication] stanza.' The vendor's Duo setup guide shows the operator choosing the name: 'externalTwoFactorAuthSettings = <2FA stanza name, usually duo-mfa>' with the stanza written '[<2FA stanza name>]'. Documentation and specification agree completely here; the assessment misread both, lifting the placeholder as a literal stanza name.

scimSupportedDomains, product disagrees with both documents. Not behind any condition, so out of scope for a verdict, but measured and worth recording: the shipped specification and the 10.4 vendor reference both state 'Default: *.okta.com, *.oktapreview.com, *.okta-emea.com', while btool on the running 10.4.2 instance reports five domains from system/default, adding *.okta-gov.com and *.okta.mil. Here it is the documentation that is stale, not the assessment.

Boolean vocabulary is undocumented. The specification types these settings '<boolean>' and neither the specification nor any vendor page I could find publishes the accepted token set. Splunk's own reference pages write 'Default: 1 (true)' and 'Default: 0 (false)', which establishes 1 and 0 as equivalent to true and false, and no more. This file nevertheless uses three different boolean vocabularies for the same type: 'in 1|true' for lockoutUsers, 'equals true' for expireUserAccounts and enableMfaAuthRest, and 'in true|True|TRUE|t|1|yes' for enablePasswordHistory. The widest of these asserts spellings the vendor does not document.
authorize.conf: Specification version mismatch, and it is the root cause of the largest defect class. The staged specification set is stamped "Version 10.0.0" and runs to 1,061 lines; the instance under assessment ships "Version 10.4.2" at 1,336 lines. Every authorize.conf line number in the citations resolves correctly in the 10.0.0 file and incorrectly in the 10.4.2 file: srchIndexesAllowed 292 vs 367, deleteIndexesAllowed 309 vs 384, srchFilter 150 vs 160, importRoles 79 vs 83, [tokens_auth] 381 vs 456, expiration 390 vs 465, [capability::admin_all_objects] 447 vs 522, [capability::change_audit] 483 vs 578, [capability::delete_by_keyword] 495 vs 590, [capability::install_apps] 760 vs 887, [capability::search] 953 vs 1088. Citations that say "confirmed present in that set" are true of 10.0.0 and unverified against the product being assessed.

The staged 10.0.0 specification carries no body text at all under [role_<roleName>] - a bare stanza header. The shipped 10.4.2 specification adds "Defines a role with the name '<roleName>'", "Role names cannot have uppercase characters", "Role names cannot contain spaces, colons, semicolons, or forward slashes" and "Role names must use valid UTF-8 character encoding". The sentence that identifies <roleName> as a site-chosen name is absent from the version the criteria were written against, which is the proximate cause of 29 of the 63 conditions being keyed to a stanza that cannot exist on any instance. Confirmed live: btool authorize list 'role_<roleName>' returns nothing and exits 0, and the assessment observations record the stanza as stanza_absent with a count of 0.

[tokens_auth] expiration contradicts itself inside a single entry, in both specification versions and on the published 10.4 documentation page: "The default value indicates that a token never expires. To set token expiration, you must set this value to a relative time value." sits four lines above "Default: +30d" (10.0.0 lines 405 and 409; 10.4.2 lines 480 and 484). Splunk's own token administration pages consistently state 30 days from issuance. The instance settles it: btool reports [tokens_auth] expiration = +30d from system/default/authorize.conf. Any criterion or fix text written from the prose sentence rather than the Default line would be wrong about the shipped state.

The authorize.conf specification presents install_apps as the capability that governs app installation, with only a cross-reference - "To enable enforcement of the 'install_apps' capability, see the 'enable_install_apps' setting in limits.conf". The limits.conf specification on the same instance (line 3588) states that enable_install_apps defaults to false and that when it is false the gate on the apps/local endpoint is admin_all_objects or edit_local_apps, not install_apps. btool confirms enable_install_apps = false from system/default/limits.conf. Read alone, as the staged set invites, authorize.conf.spec leads an assessor to write a criterion on a capability that is inert out of the box.

[capability::search] text differs between versions: 10.0.0 says only "Lets a user run a search", 10.4.2 says "Lets a user run a search using Search Processing Language (SPL) or SPL version 2 (SPL2)". Immaterial to the criterion, but it is independent evidence that the staged set is not the specification for the product under assessment.

importRoles gained two paragraphs between 10.0.0 and 10.4.2 - the configuration-precedence rule and the least-restrictive-quota rule. This matters because several citations lean on importRoles inheritance to justify or qualify capability-absence criteria, and they were written without the 10.4.2 precedence text in front of them.

The published 10.4 documentation page renders the srchIndexesDisallowed cross-reference as "deleteIndexesAlowed", one l short. Both specification files on disk, 10.0.0 and 10.4.2, spell it correctly. Cosmetic, and noted only because a key list harvested from the rendered page rather than from the .spec file would carry a setting name that does not exist - the same failure mode as the role_<roleName> criteria.

Within the shipped rule set rather than the vendor documentation, and worth recording beside the above: SRG-APP-000119-AU-000110's contribution text states the objective correctly - keep the delete path "off the general-purpose roles and away from the internal indexes" - while its own check lines test deleteIndexesAllowed against TLS protocol versions. The prose and the criteria in the same file disagree, which is how 32 TLS-contaminated conditions across six requirements survived review.
indexes.conf: The shipped specification file is the wrong version. splunk/splunk-spec-files/indexes.conf.spec declares "# Version 10.0.0" and runs 3,146 lines; the indexes.conf.spec that ships inside Splunk 10.4.2 (confirmed as build 33c3bf42cd73 on the live instance) declares "# Version 10.4.2" and runs 3,333 lines. Every citation in indexes.json carries 10.0.0 line numbers: enableDataIntegrityControl is cited at :594, which is where it sits in the 10.0.0 file; in 10.4.2 it is at :671. Likewise frozenTimePeriodInSecs cited :684 is at :761, coldToFrozenScript :713 is at :790, coldToFrozenDir :792 is at :892, homePath :412 is at :471, coldPath :446 is at :505, thawedPath :468 is at :527. Comparing the setting names in both files, 10.4.2 only adds settings (allowBulkDataMove, hashTableSize, mdlIndex, mdlRemotePath, perfTuneMetaData*, python.required, quadReloadHashTable, several remote.azure.*, remote.s3.object_locks_retention_period, tsidxSyncPeriod) and removes none, so no in-scope setting was renamed or dropped and no verdict changes on this account. The citations nonetheless do not point at the version being assessed.

coldToFrozenDir: the documentation implies no default, the product ships the key present and empty. The 10.4 indexes.conf reference block for coldToFrozenDir carries no Default line, and the 10.4 retirement and archiving page says the indexer deletes frozen data by default and that you "must tell the indexer" to archive instead. A reader of the documentation would conclude the key is absent until configured. The product's own /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/indexes.conf declares it at line 55 as `coldToFrozenDir =`, empty, and btool reports it present in all 19 index stanzas. This gap is the whole reason the `present` operator is vacuous for this setting, and no specification text discloses it.

enableDataIntegrityControl and SmartStore: the specification file is silent, the documentation is not. Neither the 10.0.0 nor the 10.4.2 indexes.conf.spec block for enableDataIntegrityControl mentions SmartStore. Vendor 10.4 documentation states "Splunk Enterprise supports data integrity control on local indexes only. There is no support on SmartStore indexes", and the 10.4 "About SmartStore" page lists it under "The following capabilities are not available for SmartStore-enabled indexes. Their corresponding settings must use their default values", with "SmartStore-enabled indexes are not compatible with the data integrity control feature". Consequence for this assessment: on a SmartStore index, the enableDataIntegrityControl condition behind SRG-APP-000080-AU-000010, SRG-APP-000369-AU-000250 and SRG-APP-000795-AU-000220 and the remote.s3.encryption condition behind SRG-APP-000231-WSR-000144 cannot both be satisfied. No rule file records that interaction.

SmartStore requires one partition for home and cold, which contradicts the separate-partition requirement. Vendor 10.4 "About SmartStore" states "The home path and cold path of each index must point to the same partition." SRG-APP-000233-WSR-000146 asks for the document directory to be on a partition separate from the system files, and the shipped criterion pursues that through homePath, coldPath and thawedPath. On a SmartStore deployment the vendor forbids part of what the criterion is reaching for. The specification file carries no such note next to the path settings.

Nothing in the collection path validates an operand against the specification, so a criterion's operand is the only guard. Measured in a throwaway btool tree (btool --dir, never under etc/): splunk btool check printed nothing and exited 0 for enableDataIntegrityControl = yes, which is outside the <boolean> vocabulary; for remote.s3.encryption = sse3, which is outside the documented sse-s3 | sse-kms | sse-c | cse | none list; and for coldToFrozenDir = volume:probe_vol/frozen, although the 10.4.2 spec states "May NOT contain a volume reference". btool read all three back verbatim. This is why not_equals none is the wrong operand for remote.s3.encryption - an enumerated `in` list is the only thing that rejects a value splunkd will not accept.

Not a conflict, recorded so it is not raised again: web search summaries twice reported that the 10.4 indexes.conf reference gives "Default: true" for enableDataIntegrityControl, conflicting with the "Manage data integrity" page's "false (off)". Reading the reference page itself, the line immediately above the enableDataIntegrityControl block is the closing "* Default: true" of the preceding setting, enableOnlineBucketRepair; the enableDataIntegrityControl block's own line reads "Default: false". The 10.4 reference, the 10.4 "Manage data integrity" page, the 10.4.2 specification shipped with the product and the live instance's system/default all agree on false. The apparent conflict is a snippet-adjacency artifact of the search tool, not a vendor disagreement.

Harness defects found while verifying, outside indexes.conf but governing these findings. (1) The collector matches stanzas literally - splunk/hardening/assess/bin/assess.sh contains `if (stanza != "" && F[1] != stanza) continue` - while every indexes.conf stanza in splunk/hardening/assess/inventory/checks.tsv is empty or a placeholder: <index>, <index name>, <index_name>, volume:<name>, volume:<volume_name>. None can equal a real stanza name, and the flattened evidence map holds real names (_audit, volume:_splunk_summaries), so literal stanzas do resolve. The same run records coldToFrozenDir as present with a value when the stanza field is empty and absent when it is <index> - one key, one instance, two answers. This is the authorize.conf role_<roleName> defect class moved from the key to the stanza. (2) The collector breaks on the first matching key, so a per-index criterion is decided from _audit alone and the other eighteen indexes are never read. (3) evaluate.sh builds its reason text from the literal placeholder stanza, so every placeholder condition reports "-> not set": SRG-APP-000080-AU-000010 reads "enableDataIntegrityControl in 1|true -> not set" while the instance has it set to false. (4) The rule file for SRG-APP-000233-WSR-000146 checks splunk-launch.conf SPLUNK_DB against TLS version patterns (matches tls1\.2, not_matches ...ssl3, tls1\.0, tls1\.1); SPLUNK_DB is a filesystem path, those four conditions can never be satisfied, and they are the only failing conditions for that requirement. (5) The rule file for SRG-APP-000760-AU-000150 carries `check: props.conf [<source type>] present`, which the parser reads as a key literally named "present" - the sole failing condition for that requirement. (6) splunk check-integrity exits 0 while reporting "Total buckets checked=2, succeeded=0, failed=2"; any harness that shells out to it must read the counters, not the exit code - the same trap as btool check.
inputs.conf: Version mismatch across the whole specification set, not just inputs.conf. The specification file the criteria were written against, splunk/splunk-spec-files/inputs.conf.spec, carries the header "# Version 10.0.0" and is 4884 lines. The assessed instance is Splunk 10.4.2 (build 33c3bf42cd73) and ships its own specification at /opt/splunk/etc/system/README/inputs.conf.spec, header "# Version 10.4.2", 4520 lines. Every line citation in the criteria resolves against the 10.0.0 file and against nothing on the instance: [splunktcp-ssl:<port>] is cited at 876 but is at 880 in 10.4.2, [SSL] at 986 but 990, [udp://<remote server>:<port>] at 1227 but 1233, [udp:<port>] at 1314 but 1320, [http] enableSSL at 1665 but 1690. The prose for every stanza in scope is unchanged between the two, so no verdict turns on this, but the citations cannot be checked against the version being assessed.

The vendor ships stanzas it does not document. /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/inputs.conf on 10.4.2 defines [udp] at line 107 and [tcp] at line 110, each with connection_host and other settings. Neither appears as a stanza in the 10.4.2 specification file or on the published 10.4.2 reference page, which document only [splunktcp] as a bare stanza alongside the port-bearing forms. Any "no UDP input is configured" criterion written as an absence test on the name udp will fail on a stock install for a stanza the vendor's own documentation does not acknowledge.

cipherSuite is documented two ways in the same entry. The 10.4.2 specification says "If not set, the input process uses the default cipher string that the OpenSSL binary provides" and then "The default can vary. See the 'cipherSuite' setting in the $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/inputs.conf file for the current default." The shipped file does set it, to an explicit ECDHE/AES/GCM and SHA-2 list, so the OpenSSL fallback never applies on a default install. The criterion's rationale cites only the OpenSSL half and therefore describes a state that does not occur.

sslVersions has no documented default, and the shipped default contradicts the criterion. The specification defers to etc/system/default/inputs.conf, which sets sslVersions = tls1.2, tls1.3. The criterion requires equals tls1.2, so the vendor's own default is a finding and the only remediation is removing TLS 1.3.

The vendor's worked example in inputs.conf.spec, reproduced on the published 10.4.2 page, configures [SSL] with serverCert, the DEPRECATED password setting rather than sslPassword, and requireClientCert=false, followed by the bare stanza [splunktcp-ssl:9996]. It is an example the product benchmark would fail, and it shows the single-colon port spelling, while this instance uses [splunktcp-ssl://9997]. Criteria written against the literal placeholder splunktcp-ssl:<port> match neither spelling.

disabled is tested in a stanza where the vendor does not declare it. The 10.4.2 specification documents disabled = <boolean> in twelve stanzas, none of them a TCP or UDP receiving stanza; the criteria test it under [udp:<port>].

requireClientCert has no single documented default - "false with self-signed and third-party certificates", "true with the default certificates, overriding the existing false setting" - so no criterion may treat an absent value as a known state, in either direction.

[splunktcp-ssl:<port>] documents acceptFrom only by cross-reference and omits the default line that the sibling [tcp-ssl:<port>] states as "Default: '*' (accept from anywhere)". Whether a global [splunktcp] acceptFrom is inherited by splunktcp-ssl ports is not stated anywhere in the specification or on the published page, and the instance cannot settle it without changing a listener; it remains undetermined.
outputs.conf: cipherSuite, scope: the shipped outputs.conf.spec (10.4.2, line 664) describes it as "The specified cipher string for the input processors" and says it "ensures that the server does not accept connections using weak encryption protocols" - server-side, input-side wording inside a file the same spec opens by saying "Forwarders require outputs.conf. Splunk instances that do not forward do not use it." The published guide instead presents cipherSuite as the suites this instance offers as a TLS client. The assessor quoted the spec's server-side wording as the rationale for the outputs.conf condition.

cipherSuite, TLS version reach: the published page states "The cipherSuite setting controls TLS 1.2 cipher suites" and that TLS 1.3 suites are set in a [tls1.3] stanza that "exists only in server.conf", whose cipherSuite "accepts only TLS 1.3 cipher suite names and does not accept TLS 1.2 cipher suite names". The shipped outputs.conf.spec says none of this: its sslVersions entry (line 797) lists tls1.3 as available while its cipherSuite entry (line 664) never says the setting cannot reach TLS 1.3. An assessor working only from the spec file would reasonably conclude, as this one did, that TLS 1.3 suite names belong in outputs.conf cipherSuite.

sslPassword, what it is the password for: outputs.conf.spec:647-650 says "The password associated with the Certificate Authority certificate (CAcert)" and "The default Splunk CAcert uses the password 'password'". The published forwarding-TLS page describes it as the password for the private key and says not to configure the setting when no password was set on the private key. The spec gives no such carve-out, which is what makes a non_empty condition look safe.

sslPassword, where it belongs: the spec's GLOBAL SETTINGS preamble says not to set sslPassword in the [default] stanza and to "specify these settings in the [tcpout] stanza instead". The published forwarding-TLS page and product STIG SPLK-CL-000460 both place it in a [tcpout:<target_group>] stanza. The spec and the guide point at different stanzas for the same setting.

useSSL: outputs.conf.spec:635-645 documents useSSL = <true|false|legacy>, Default: legacy, as the setting that decides whether the forwarder uses TLS. The published 10.4 pages "Configure Splunk indexing and forwarding to use TLS certificates" and "Configure TLS protocol version support..." do not mention useSSL at all; they present clientCert as the means of securing the connection. The non-deprecated, unambiguous way to require TLS on the forwarding channel exists in the spec and is missing from the prose documentation.

Shipped default vs shipped TLS library: /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/outputs.conf sets cipherSuite with four ECDH-ECDSA-* suites (ECDH-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, ECDH-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256, ECDH-ECDSA-AES256-SHA384, ECDH-ECDSA-AES128-SHA256). The bundled OpenSSL 3.5.7 rejects each one individually ("no cipher match") and silently drops all four from the merged list, leaving 14 of 15 tokens plus the three always-on TLS 1.3 suites. The vendor's own default contains four dead cipher names.

sslVersions coverage: the published "Configure TLS protocol version support for secure connections between Splunk platform instances" page lists inputs.conf [SSL] and server.conf [sslConfig] in its component table and does not list outputs.conf, although the 10.4 outputs.conf reference documents sslVersions for the forwarding connection and the shipped default file sets it to tls1.2, tls1.3.

Product STIG vs vendor version support: SPLK-CL-000430 (Splunk Enterprise 8.x for Linux STIG V2R3, benchmarks/U_Splunk_Enterprise_8-x_for_Linux_STIG_V2R3_Manual-xccdf.xml) prescribes sslVersions = tls1.2 for outputs.conf. The 10.4 documentation states "Version 1.3 of the TLS protocol is available starting in Splunk Enterprise version 10.4.0" and that the default "changes from tls1.2 to tls1.2,tls1.3". An 8.x value was carried into a 10.4 assessment where it now excludes the newer approved version. Separately, that STIG's fix text is conditional - "If the following lines do not exist, then the settings are compliant. If they exist, they must match the settings below or be removed" - and the criteria converted it into a mandatory equality, inverting the benchmark's own logic.

btool check validates key names only: measured on the running 10.4.2 instance with a throwaway etc tree, btool check rejected bogusSettingName and server-in-[tcpout] but accepted useACK = banana and sslVersions = tls9.9. No vendor page states this limitation, yet btool is the tool the product STIG check texts imply for verifying these settings. Any criterion whose correctness rests on a value being rejected cannot be proven with btool.
savedsearches.conf: STANZA, THE DEFECT THAT TOUCHES ALL 66 CONDITIONS. Every condition is anchored to [<stanza name>] (57), [<search name>] (8), [<search_name>] (8) or to no stanza at all (6). The live 10.4.2 spec file contains exactly ONE stanza header, at line 31: '[<stanza name>]', followed by 'Create a unique stanza name for each saved search.' It is the specification's placeholder, the same class of defect as the authorize.conf 'role_<roleName>' key. Measured: `btool savedsearches list --debug | grep -cE '\[<stanza name>\]|\[<search name>\]|\[<search_name>\]'` returns 0 against 182 real stanzas. '<search name>' and '<search_name>' are not even the spec's notation - they appear nowhere in the 10.4.2 or 10.0.0 spec file. Unlike 'role_<roleName>', a literal stanza named [<stanza name>] IS syntactically legal (savedsearches stanza names are free-form; a probe stanza with that literal name parsed and btool check exited 0), so these conditions are not unparseable - they are unmeetable, because no installation names a saved search '<stanza name>'. Every Open finding they produced is an artifact of the placeholder, not of the configuration.

SHIPPED SPEC IS 10.0.0, THE TARGET IS 10.4.2. splunk/splunk-spec-files/savedsearches.conf.spec is stamped '#   Version 10.0.0' at line 1; the instance's own spec is stamped '#   Version 10.4.2'. The 11 entries are byte-identical between the two (diffed entry by entry, all IDENTICAL), so there is no semantic drift - but every cited line number is wrong for 10.4.2: enableSched 73 -> 86, cron_schedule 79 -> 92, schedule_window 193 -> 228, counttype 249 -> 284, alert_condition 270 -> 305, action.email 300 -> 335, action.email.to 304 -> 339, action.email.sendpdf 383 -> 418, dispatch.earliest_time 564 -> 599, dispatch.latest_time 571 -> 606. Only [<stanza name>] (31) and search (44) still land. One citation asserts 'The staged specification set is stamped Version 10.0.0; every key and value cited was confirmed present in that set' - true, and the wrong set to confirm against.

COUNTTYPE=CUSTOM HAS NO CURRENT VENDOR SUPPORT. The criterion's rationale says 'custom is the value under which the alert fires on the stated alert_condition rather than on every run.' No vendor source says this. Older spec text (8.x/9.x era) said the opposite - 'If you specify an alert_condition, do not set counttype, relation, or quantity' - and a Splunk staff answer confirmed it and said earlier documentation stating otherwise had been corrected (community.splunk.com returned 403 to direct fetch, so this is from search summaries, not a quote I verified myself). Neither the shipped 10.0.0 spec, the live 10.4.2 spec, nor the published 10.0 and 10.4 pages contain that sentence: grep for 'alert_condition' in the live spec returns one hit, line 305, and the only co-occurrence rule anywhere is counttype's own 'NOTE: If you specify "always," do not set relation or quantity.' So the vendor has withdrawn the rule in both directions and documents no counttype/alert_condition dependency at all in 10.4.2.

PRESENT IS A VACUOUS OPERATOR FOR THREE OF THESE SETTINGS. $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/savedsearches.conf ships dispatch.earliest_time = (empty), dispatch.latest_time = (empty) and schedule_window = 0. Measured against effective configuration: all three keys are present in 182 of 182 stanzas. Any condition written as 'present' is satisfied by the shipped default for every saved search on every installation and can never produce a finding - yet seven conditions use it (3 x dispatch.earliest_time, 4 x dispatch.latest_time, 2 x schedule_window, less overlap). The rationale for dispatch.earliest_time even states the window 'must be stated rather than left unbounded', which 'present' does not test: present-with-empty-value bounds nothing.

SCHEDULE_WINDOW HAS TWO DOCUMENTED DEFAULTS, NEITHER OF WHICH IS 'UNSET'. The 10.4.2 spec gives 'Default: 0 for searches that are owned by users with the edit_search_schedule_window capability' and 'Default: auto for searches that are owned by users that do not have the edit_search_schedule_window capability. For these searches, this setting cannot be changed.' The criterion treats an unset schedule_window as a gap; the vendor documents it as always defined, and for users without that capability not changeable at all - so the condition can be unsatisfiable by design for those owners. The spec also warns 'A non-zero schedule_window is mutually exclusive with a non-default schedule_priority', so mandating it can conflict with another setting.

ACTION.EMAIL.SENDPDF'S DEFAULT IS NOT LOCAL TO THIS FILE. The documented default is '0 (false) (or the sendpdf setting in the alert_actions.conf file)'. A criterion that reads only savedsearches.conf cannot determine the delivered form of a report, because alert_actions.conf can supply it. The spec also carries five form switches, not one - action.email.inline, .sendcsv, .sendpdf, .sendpng, .sendresults (lines 399, 405, 418, 423, 428). There is no action.email.format in savedsearches.conf 10.4.2.

BTOOL CHECK VALIDATES NOTHING IN THIS FILE. A probe app carrying enableSched = 7, counttype = bogusvalue, action.email = maybe, action.email.sendpdf = 3, schedule_window = notanumber and dispatch.earliest_time = ThisIsNotATime was parsed without complaint: `splunk btool check` exited 0 and its output mentioned the probe app zero times. btool savedsearches list read every garbage value back verbatim. No vendor page claims btool validates value vocabulary, and none of these operands can be confirmed by a btool-based check.

ENABLESCHED ACCEPTS A VALUE ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION FORBIDS. The spec and the published 10.4 page both say 'The only acceptable values for this setting are 0 and 1.' Measured: 'enableSched = true' was accepted into the file and read back by btool as 'true', not normalized to 1. The same held for action.email = true and action.email.sendpdf = true. Whether splunkd honors the word form at run time is untested - it needs an authenticated REST call or a restart, both out of bounds here.

EMAIL NOTIFICATION DEPENDS ON A SERVER SPLUNK DOES NOT SHIP. alert_actions.conf.spec states the SMTP server 'is not included with the Splunk instance' and defaults mailserver to localhost. Measured on the instance: action.email = 1 on 0 of 182 stanzas, and action.email.to appears 0 times in the entire effective configuration. The 19 conditions on action.email and action.email.to therefore test the organization's mail infrastructure and its recipient roster, not the application's configurable share - that belongs in external_dependencies under the assessment's own scope rule.

SIX CONDITIONS CARRY NO STANZA AT ALL AND WERE SCORED AGAINST THE GLOBAL DEFAULT LAYER. For SRG-APP-000516-AU-000350 and -000360 the observed values recorded are 'enableSched -> is 0', 'cron_schedule -> is ', 'action.email -> is 0' - which are exactly etc/system/default/savedsearches.conf. A stanza-less condition on this file resolves to the [default] layer, where enableSched = 1 would schedule all 182 saved searches at once. That is a load event, not a hardening step.

THE ASSESSMENT ALREADY REACHED THE RIGHT CONCLUSION FOR ALERT_CONDITION AND THEN DID NOT APPLY IT. The citation text for SRG-APP-000293-AU-000430 and -000294-AU-000440 states that alert_condition non_empty 'reports a finding against a working alert' because counttype with relation and quantity is the other trigger form, and the condition was removed there. The identical condition was left in place for SRG-APP-000359-WSR-000065, SRG-APP-000360-AU-000130, SRG-APP-000795-AU-000220 and SRG-APP-000795-WSR-000130.

SEVERAL OBSERVED VALUES BELONG TO OTHER FILES. The recorded observations read 'savedsearches.conf [<search name>] enableSched equals 1 -> is splunk' and '-> is localhost' (those are alert_actions.conf [email] from = splunk and mailserver = localhost), '-> is 5000' for three conditions under SRG-APP-000359-WSR-000065, and '-> is web_access.log' for four under SRG-APP-000795-WSR-000130 (that is web.conf log.access_file). No savedsearches.conf setting in scope can hold any of those values. Whatever produced these observations read a value from a different file and attributed it to this one, so the Open verdicts resting on them are not evidence about savedsearches.conf at all.
server.conf: VERSION MISMATCH AT THE ROOT. The specification file the assessment cites, splunk-spec-files/server.conf.spec, carries the header "# Version 10.0.0" and is 6645 lines. The instance under assessment ships "# Version 10.4.2" at 7423 lines ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/README/server.conf.spec); a whitespace-normalized diff is 1041 lines. Every line-number citation in internal_dev/verify2/server.json points into the 10.0.0 file and does not resolve in 10.4.2 (for example the assessment's :1125 for certificateStatusValidationMethod is :1162 in 10.4.2, and :5392 for [kvstore] sslCRLPath is :5641).

sslVersions VOCABULARY. Shipped 10.0.0 spec: 'The versions available are "ssl3", "tls1.0", "tls1.1", and "tls1.2".' 10.4.2 spec: 'The versions available are "tls1.0", "tls1.1", "tls1.2", and "tls1.3".' plus 'SSL versions 2 and 3 are always disabled.' The 10.4 vendor page states SSLv3 'Support removed in version 10.4.0 of Splunk Enterprise' and lists it as 'Not supported'. Every criterion operand built from the ssl3/tls1.0/tls1.1/tls1.2 vocabulary is written against a version set the product no longer has.

tls1.3 IS ABSENT FROM THE SHIPPED SPEC. The string 'tls1.3' occurs zero times in splunk-spec-files/server.conf.spec. The 10.4.2 spec adds an entire [tls1.3] stanza (line 1293) with its own cipherSuite and groups settings, and the vendor states 'Version 1.3 of the TLS protocol is available starting in Splunk Enterprise version 10.4.0' and is 'Active alongside TLS 1.2 by default'. The assessment could not have seen TLS 1.3 and its conditions reflect that.

THE VENDOR DEFAULT IS STRONGER THAN THE CRITERIA. $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf on the 10.4.2 instance sets, at lines 163-164, 'sslVersions = tls1.2, tls1.3' and 'sslVersionsForClient = tls1.2, tls1.3'. The inter-Splunk vendor page states 'The default at version 10.4.0 and higher is tls1.2,tls1.3.' Criteria that pin these keys to exactly tls1.2 reject the vendor default.

deprecatedTlsVersionSupport IS NOT IN THE SHIPPED SPEC. The 10.4.2 spec defines 'deprecatedTlsVersionSupport = <boolean>' at line 795 under [sslConfig], 'Default: false', controlling 'Whether or not the Splunk platform supports the "tls1.0" and "tls1.1" TLS protocol versions.' It occurs zero times in splunk-spec-files/server.conf.spec. The running instance logs at every startup: 'Deprecated TLS protocol versions 1.0 (tls1.0) and 1.1 (tls1.1) are not available for configuration because support for them was explicitly turned off through the deprecatedTlsVersionSupport setting.' This is the setting that actually floors the protocol version on 10.4.2, and no condition in the assessment names it.

FIPS CLAUSE REMOVED. Shipped 10.0.0 spec, under sslVersions: 'If the Splunk platform instance runs in FIPS mode, "ssl3" is always disabled regardless of this configuration.' 10.4.2 replaces this with the unconditional 'SSL versions 2 and 3 are always disabled.' The assessment's FIPS-linked rationale for the ssl3 exclusions rests on a sentence the product no longer carries.

cipherSuite SCOPE. The 10.4 vendor page states the [sslConfig] cipherSuite setting 'does not apply to TLS 1.3 connections' and 'To configure TLS 1.3 cipher suites, use the [tls1.3] stanza', and that 'the cipherSuite setting in [tls1.3] accepts only TLS 1.3 cipher suite names' and 'does not accept TLS 1.2 cipher suite names.' Neither the shipped 10.0.0 spec nor the assessment makes this split, and the assessment's cipherSuite regex mixes both name forms into one [sslConfig] value.

ecdhCurves SCOPE AND FIPS. The vendor states 'The ecdhCurves setting in [sslConfig] controls key exchange curves for TLS 1.2 connections' and 'For TLS 1.3 connections, the equivalent setting is groups in the [tls1.3] stanza.' It also states 'Only AES-GCM cipher suites and the secp384r1 and secp256r1 curves are FIPS 140-3 approved.' The assessment pins a curve list containing secp521r1 while other conditions in the same assessment require FIPS mode.

remote.s3.encryption STANZA. In 10.4.2 server.conf this setting is defined only at line 6718, inside the [search_artifact_remote_storage] stanza (header at line 6461). The assessment's condition carries an empty stanza, so it names no stanza at all. For index data at rest the setting belongs to a volume stanza in indexes.conf, not server.conf.

sessionTimeout DEFAULT NOTATION. Both specs and the 10.4 vendor reference document 'Default: "1" (1 hour)', but the shipped default file writes 'sessionTimeout = 1h'. Any criterion matching the documented bare-integer form must also accept the form the product actually ships.

allowRemoteLogin IS DEPRECATED AT THE VALUE THE CRITERION ACCEPTS. The 10.4.2 spec states 'NOTE: As of version 7.1, Splunk software does not support the use of default passwords. The "requireSetPassword" value is deprecated and might be removed in the future.' The assessment treats requireSetPassword as a compliant value without recording that it is deprecated and, since 7.1, restricts nothing.

CRL PATH PLACEMENT. The 10.4.2 [sslConfig] certificateStatusValidationMethod entry cross-references '[kvstore]:sslCRLPath' as the instance-wide CRL guidance, and the [kvstore] sslCRLPath entry describes splunkd (not KV store) as the consumer. The assessment reached the same conclusion, but from 10.0.0 line numbers that no longer resolve.
splunk-launch.conf: SPLUNK_FIPS vocabulary. The shipped specification declares SPLUNK_FIPS = [0|1] with Default: 0, and the vendor's 10.4 reference page says the same. The product disagrees with both. On 10.4.2 the launcher accepts case-insensitive 1, 0, true, false, t, f, yes and no, and aborts with "SPLUNK_FIPS setting has been set to a bad value" on 2, -1, on, off, y, n, enabled and disabled. The documented vocabulary is narrower than the implemented one, and every criterion written as `equals 1` inherits that error.

SPLUNK_FIPS self-contradiction inside one spec entry. splunk-launch.conf.spec:110 declares the vocabulary as [0|1] and line 131 gives Default: 0, while lines 119-128 of the same entry instruct the operator to configure the setting to "true", warn that a kernel in FIPS mode makes it "true" by default, and state it cannot later be configured to "false". The vendor's 10.4 FIPS guide meanwhile instructs the literal line SPLUNK_FIPS=1 and never mentions true. Three vendor sources, three spellings, for one setting.

SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA is undocumented yet real. The setting is absent from the vendor's splunk-launch.conf reference in every edition checked (9.0, 9.1, 9.2, 10.0 and 10.4), absent from the 10.4 FIPS guide, and absent from the 10.4 FIPS and Common Criteria best-practice page. It nonetheless exists in 10.4.2: the literal appears in /opt/splunk/bin/splunkd and /opt/splunk/bin/splunk, and the specification shipped in the same build documents it indirectly at server.conf.spec:5646-5648 as the condition under which splunkd uses the CRL file. An operator directed to set it has no file reference entry to work from.

No 10.x Common Criteria manual exists for the manual the shipped spec cites. splunk-launch.conf.spec:60-64 and server.conf.spec:5654-5656 both refer the operator to a "Securing Splunk Enterprise for Common Criteria" manual for the certification status. The most recent edition I could find is 9.2, and the vendor's own 10.4 best-practice page links that 9.2 edition. The 9.2 manual restricts Common Criteria mode to a single instance on a single machine with no support for distributed deployments.

Common Criteria support status contradicts across vendor material. The specifications shipped inside 10.4.2 state at splunk-launch.conf.spec:60 and server.conf.spec:5654 that "Splunk supports using the product in Common Criteria mode" for NIAP-certified configurations only, while the vendor's published 10.0 authentication.conf reference still states that Splunk does not support the product in Common Criteria mode until NIAP has certified it. The 9.0 and 9.2 splunk-launch.conf pages carry the older wording as well.

SPLUNK_BINDIP self-contradiction on Splunk Web. splunk-launch.conf.spec:80 says the address is what "splunkd and splunkweb should bind to", while lines 93-94 of the same entry say it "Does not override web.conf/[settings]/server.socket_host for SplunkWeb if set". The vendor's published 10.4 page carries the first claim. The assessor's rationale relies on the splunkd half, lines 88-89, which is the part both sources agree on.

SPLUNK_BINDIP vocabulary is documented but not enforced. The spec and the vendor page both declare <ip address>. On 10.4.2 the launcher accepted the literal string not-an-ip and 999.999.999.999 at rc=0. A `non_empty` criterion over an unvalidated setting therefore proves nothing about what the listeners bind to.

An undocumented FIPS prerequisite. splunkd on 10.4.2 carries the string "Failed to enable FIPS support: OPENSSL_CONF is not set". Neither the splunk-launch.conf.spec SPLUNK_FIPS entry nor the vendor's 10.4 page or FIPS guide mentions that OPENSSL_CONF must be set for FIPS mode to come up. This instance happens to set it.

The shipped assessment specification models splunk-launch.conf as a stanza-and-key file. Every condition carries a stanza field, inconsistently "" on the first and null on the other twenty-three, and the evidence strings render as "splunk-launch.conf [] KEY ...", implying an empty-named stanza. The vendor states the opposite at splunk-launch.conf.spec:7-11 and on the published page: there is only one such file in the whole system, at $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/splunk-launch.conf, "there are no stanzas, explicit or implicit", and copies under etc/apps or etc/users are ignored. The stanza field should be absent, not empty.

The documented collection method cannot read this file, which is how all twenty-four conditions came to read "not set". On the 10.4.2 instance `splunk btool splunk-launch list --debug` returns zero lines at exit 0, although SPLUNK_HOME is set in /opt/splunk/etc/splunk-launch.conf, confirmed by grep. A deliberately bogus name, `splunk btool zzz_does_not_exist list`, also returns zero lines at exit 0, so an empty result cannot be told apart from an unsupported file. btool is blind to splunk-launch.conf because the file is outside the configuration layering, exactly as the vendor documents. Any harness that evaluates these conditions through btool will report every setting in this file as not set whatever the file contains. `splunk envvars` does read the file and is the correct read-only source: it reported SPLUNK_DB, SPLUNK_SERVER_NAME, PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY, PYTHONUTF8 and ENABLE_CPUSHARES on this instance. Four of the six settings in scope are genuinely absent here, so most verdicts survive, but they were not actually measured.

Citation line numbers for OPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_FILE_LOCKING are wrong. The shipped specification cites splunk-launch.conf.spec:214-220; in the 10.4.2 spec that range is the caution prose and the setting is defined at lines 226-233. The quoted caution text itself is accurate, and the SPLUNK_FIPS citation at line 110 is exact, so the specification is keyed to the correct spec file and this reference alone is off.

The product STIG underpinning most of these rationales is two major versions behind. SPLK-CL-000390 and SPLK-CL-000430 come from U_Splunk_Enterprise_8-x_for_Linux_STIG_V2R3, confirmed in the local benchmark copy, and the fix text does literally prescribe SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA=1 and SPLUNK_FIPS=1 as the assessor quoted. Applied to 10.4.2 that fix text prescribes one setting the vendor no longer documents and a FIPS value narrower than what 10.4.2 accepts. It also predates SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION, which 10.4.2 defaults to 140-2, a standard the shipped spec records NIST as planning to retire by September 2026, so a FIPS condition that ignores SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION leaves the instance on the retiring standard while scoring compliant.
web.conf: The specification file shipped in the repository (splunk-spec-files/web.conf.spec) is "# Version 10.0.0"; the instance under assessment is Splunk 10.4.2 (build 33c3bf42cd73) and its own /opt/splunk/etc/system/README/web.conf.spec is "# Version 10.4.2". Every citation in verify2/web.json carries 10.0.0 line numbers, which do not address the 10.4.2 text (for example maxThreads/maxSockets are cited at 1098-1112 but sit at 1153/1161 in 10.4.2). The two files differ substantively, not only in numbering, as the entries below show.

sslVersions: the 10.0.0 spec states the available versions are "ssl3", "tls1.0", "tls1.1" and "tls1.2". The 10.4.2 spec states they are "tls1.0", "tls1.1", "tls1.2" and "tls1.3" and that "SSL versions 2 and 3 are always disabled." The vendor TLS page adds that TLS 1.3 is supported from 10.4.0 and is on by default with TLS 1.2, and that TLS 1.0/1.1 are off by default. Every sslVersions criterion in web.json was built from the 10.0.0 vocabulary and has no tls1.3 token.

cookieSameSite: the 10.0.0 spec states "Default: not_specified". The 10.4.2 spec states "Default: lax" and the shipped 10.4.2 etc/system/default/web.conf sets cookieSameSite = lax. The criterion 'in lax|strict' is a real gap under the 10.0.0 default and already satisfied under the 10.4.2 default.

allowSslCompression: the 10.4.2 spec adds "In Splunk Enterprise version 10.4 and later, this setting has no effect when TLS 1.3 is enabled. TLS 1.3 does not support SSL-layer compression." The 10.0.0 spec carries no such statement. Since TLS 1.3 is on by default in 10.4.2 (confirmed live), the setting the criterion tests has no effect on the objective.

SSOMode: the 10.4.2 shipped spec declares the value list as "[permissive | strict]" and then states "Default: lax" - a value that is not in its own list. The 10.0.0 spec states "Default: strict", the vendor 10.4 web.conf reference page states the default is strict, and the shipped 10.4.2 default file sets SSOMode = strict. The 10.4.2 spec is wrong on its own face.

mgmtHostPort: both spec files and the vendor 10.4 web.conf reference page state "Default (on all other Splunk platform instance types): 0.0.0.0:8089", and the Bind Splunk to an IP page repeats that the default is 0.0.0.0:8089. The shipped 10.4.2 etc/system/default/web.conf sets mgmtHostPort = 127.0.0.1:8089. The documented default and the shipped default disagree.

mgmtHostPort semantics: both spec files state "The port listens on all avalible host IP addresses (0.0.0.0)" (vendor typo retained). This contradicts the assessment's use of a loopback value in this setting as an exposure control, and the live instance confirms the vendor: the setting is 127.0.0.1:8089 while splunkd's management socket is bound to 0.0.0.0:8089.

cipherSuite and ecdhCurves scope: the vendor page About TLS encryption and cipher suites states "The cipherSuite setting controls TLS 1.2 cipher suites" and that TLS 1.3 suites are configured in the [tls1.3] stanza of server.conf, whose cipherSuite key "accepts only TLS 1.3 cipher suite names and does not accept TLS 1.2 cipher suite names"; for ecdhCurves it states the TLS 1.3 equivalent is 'groups' in [tls1.3]. Neither spec file records that web.conf cipherSuite and ecdhCurves govern TLS 1.2 only, so both criteria silently leave the TLS 1.3 half of a 10.4.2 listener ungoverned.

Session timeout arithmetic: the vendor page Configure user session timeouts states that the splunkweb/splunkd countdown "does not begin until the browser session reaches its timeout value" and that to get the total you "add the value of ui_inactivity_timeout to the smaller of the timeout values for splunkweb and splunkd", with the worked example "The user session stays active for 25 minutes (15m+10m)". Neither spec file states the additive relationship; the 10.4.2 spec says only that the countdown "effectively resets every minute through browser activity until the 'ui_inactivity_timeout' setting is reached". The criteria bound each key at 15 independently, which yields a 30-minute window.

CAC authentication versus SSOMode: the vendor 10.4 CAC page requires SSOMode = permissive and trustedIP = 127.0.0.1, and states that LDAP is required and "No other scheme type, including native authentication, works for this purpose." The assessment's condition web.conf [settings] SSOMode not_equals permissive (SRG-APP-000223-WSR-000145) is therefore mutually unsatisfiable with the seven conditions that require enableCertBasedUserAuth and requireClientCert to be true. Neither spec file states the SSOMode dependency.

certBasedUserAuthPivOidList: the vendor CAC page gives the default as "1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.3, Microsoft Universal Principal Name". The shipped 10.4.2 default adds a third entry: "Microsoft User Principal Name".

pid_path: both spec files state it "Must be set to 'var/run/splunk/splunkweb.pid'" and "CAUTION: Do not change this parameter." In the shipped 10.4.2 default web.conf the line is commented out (line 428), and the running instance creates no splunkweb.pid - only splunkd.pid and conf-mutator.pid exist, because the appserver runs as a child of splunkd rather than as a separate splunkweb process.

alert_actions.conf\temail\temail.live_evidence: podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool alert_actions list email | grep -c '^email *=' returned 0. A grep for '^email *=' across /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf, /opt/splunk/etc/system/local/alert_actions.conf and every /opt/splunk/etc/apps/*/{default,local}/alert_actions.conf returned 0. btool alert_actions list --debug shows the full merged [email] stanza with no such key.
alert_actions.conf\temail\temail.notes: This is the same defect class as the role_<roleName> criterion: the stanza name was written into the key field. The rationale says the row is marked key_status=stanza, so a stanza-presence check was intended. That intent is also unfalsifiable, because /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf ships [email] on every install, so the merged configuration always contains it. The correction substitutes the one part of this file that can actually fail for this requirement. The alerting path for a processing failure is otherwise driven by health.conf [health_reporter] alert.actions, and the existence of a reachable SMTP relay is external to the product.
alert_actions.conf\temail\temail.vendor_says: There is no setting named "email" anywhere in alert_actions.conf. "email" is the name of the stanza. The documented [email] settings are from, to, cc, bcc, allowedDomainList, message.report, message.alert, subject, subject.alert, subject.report, useNSSubject, escapeCSVNewline, newLineValuesInCSV, footer.text, format, include.*, content_type, sendresults, inline, priority, mailserver, use_ssl, use_tls, auth_username, auth_password, oauth_*, sendpdf, sendcsv, sendpng, allow_empty_attachment, pdfview, report*, width_sort_columns, preprocess_results, pdf.*, sslVersions, sslVerifyServerCert, sslVerifyServerName, sslCommonNameToCheck, sslAltNameToCheck, cipherSuite. The stanza header reads: "[email] * Set email notification options under this stanza name."

alert_actions.conf\temail\tfrom.live_evidence: podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool alert_actions list email returns "from = splunk", sourced under --debug from /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf.
alert_actions.conf\temail\tfrom.notes: The criterion argues against itself. Its own rationale says "the default sender is the bare word splunk, not a routable address", yet the operator chosen is non_empty, which the bare word splunk satisfies. The condition passes on a stock install and so never tests the thing the rationale identifies. A pattern operator is the only way to express the stated intent in this file.
alert_actions.conf\temail\tfrom.vendor_says: "from = <string>", "Email address from which the alert originates.", "Default: splunk". Same text in the 10.4.2 spec on the instance at line 182.

alert_actions.conf\temail\tmailserver.live_evidence: podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool alert_actions list email returns "mailserver = localhost"; with --debug the source is /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf, i.e. the untouched product default. The same host also shows disabled = 1 and allowedDomainList = localhost from /opt/splunk/etc/system/local/alert_actions.conf, and use_ssl = 0, use_tls = 0.
alert_actions.conf\temail\tmailserver.notes: The setting exists and the rationale reads the vendor text correctly, but non_empty is satisfied by the documented default localhost, so the condition passes on an install where no relay has been named at all. It therefore cannot detect the state the rationale describes. Two further limits on this condition: the vendor states outright that the SMTP server "is not included with the Splunk instance", so whether a relay actually exists and accepts the mail belongs in external_dependencies, not in a condition; and on this instance allowedDomainList = localhost means the vendor-documented behavior is to silently strip any recipient outside that domain, so satisfying this condition would still not deliver a notification. A site that deliberately relays through a local MTA would be flagged by the corrected condition, which should be recorded as a documentable exception rather than softened back to non_empty.
alert_actions.conf\temail\tmailserver.vendor_says: "mailserver = <host>[:<port>]", "You must have a Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server available to send email. This is not included with the Splunk instance.", "Specifies the SMTP mail server to use when sending emails.", "When the 'use_ssl' setting (see below) is set to 1 (true), you must specify both <host> and <port>.", "Default: localhost". Same text in the 10.4.2 spec on the instance at line 312.

alert_actions.conf\temail\tsslVerifyServ.correction: alert_actions.conf [email] use_tls in 1|true (added alongside the existing sslVerifyServerCert in 1|true condition)
alert_actions.conf\temail\tsslVerifyServ.live_evidence: The key does not appear in /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/alert_actions.conf: btool alert_actions list email | grep -c '^sslVerifyServerCert' returns 0, so the effective value is the spec default false. The documented prerequisite is met on this host: btool server list sslConfig returns sslRootCAPath = /opt/splunk/etc/auth/labcerts/ca.pem. But the mail channel is plaintext: btool alert_actions list email returns use_ssl = 0 and use_tls = 0.
alert_actions.conf\temail\tsslVerifyServ.notes: The setting exists, true is inside the boolean vocabulary, and the rationale describes what it does accurately. The defect is that it cannot carry the requirement alone: certificate verification only happens inside a TLS session, and the vendor ships use_ssl = 0 and use_tls = 0, which is also what the instance resolves to. Setting sslVerifyServerCert = true on this host changes nothing about the transmission, so meeting the condition does not maintain confidentiality during preparation for transmission. The vendor's own [email] example pairs the three settings together, which is the configuration the condition set should require. Replace the SRG-APP-000429-WSR-000113 operand ^SHA512-crypt(-[0-9]+)?$ with it, and add to all five an external_dependencies note that existing stored hashes are not re-hashed by this setting.

I checked the stock value against all four regexes used in this file: SHA512-crypt matches ^SHA(256|512)-crypt(-[0-9]{4,})?$, ^SHA512-crypt(-[0-9]+)?$ and ^SHA(256|512)-crypt(-[1-9][0-9]{3,})?$, because the rounds group is optional in each. So all five conditions over this setting already pass on a stock 10.4.2 instance.
authentication.conf\tauthentication\tpas.notes: The setting exists exactly where the criteria say, and the vocabulary and default are confirmed by both the 10.4 reference and the instance. Three defects, in order of weight. First, SRG-APP-000429-WSR-000113's regex ^SHA512-crypt(-[0-9]+)?$ admits SHA512-crypt-1, a round count the vendor states must be at least 1000; the SRG-APP-000610-AU-000050 regex ^SHA(256|512)-crypt(-[1-9][0-9]{3,})?$ enforces the floor properly and is the one to standardize on. Second, that same regex excludes SHA256-crypt, which is no less FIPS-approved than SHA512-crypt for the stated objective of encrypting stored credentials; narrowing to SHA512 is a preference, not a requirement, and it conflicts with the other four conditions on the same setting. Third, and documented by the vendor but absent from every rationale here: the setting 'only affects new password settings... Existing passwords work but retain their previous hashing algorithm', so configuring it does not remediate credentials already stored, and the forced re-hash of existing accounts is an operator action belonging in external_dependencies. Finally, all five conditions are already satisfied by the stock default of SHA512-crypt and contribute nothing to their findings, which are Open on splunk-launch.conf SPLUNK_FIPS instead; the observed_reason fields confirm this.

The number of rounds must be at least 1000... * This setting only affects new password settings (either when a user is added or a user's password is changed). Existing passwords work but retain their previous hashing algorithm. * Default: SHA512-crypt'.

Those are different controls: history would happily accept a password that has never been used on the instance and sits at the top of every breach list. The product STIG SPLK-CL-000410 makes the same mapping, so the assessor followed it faithfully and the citation is accurate; the mapping itself is what does not hold against the vendor's description of the setting. authorize.conf\trole_user, role_power\ts.live_evidence: podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool authorize list --debug: [role_user] srchIndexesAllowed = * and [role_power] srchIndexesAllowed = *, both from /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/authorize.conf. Every srchIndexesAllowed value present anywhere on the instance is an index expression: *, *;_*, *;_audit;_internal;_metrics;..., epo_all. btool indexes list shows the indexes are _audit, _internal, _introspection, _metrics, main, epo_all, history, summary and the rest - there is no index named tls1.2, tls1.1, tls1.0 or ssl3, so "matches tls1\.2" can never be satisfied and the three not_matches conditions pass on every instance that will ever exist.
authorize.conf\trole_user, role_power\ts.notes: The operand and the rationale both belong to a different setting. The rationale reads "the version list must offer TLS 1.2" and "a leading '-' excludes a version, so only an unprefixed entry counts" - that is the vocabulary of sslVersions in server.conf and web.conf, carried into an index allow-list. Eight conditions across the two requirements are affected: one unsatisfiable matches and three vacuous not_matches per stanza pair. Under the corrected condition the instance passes: role_user and role_power ship "*", and the vendor states "*" does not match internal indexes, so neither general-purpose role can read _audit by default. The authorize.conf share of both findings is therefore false once the criterion is fixed. The accept test for the operand (writing srchIndexesAllowed into a throwaway conf through the REST configs endpoint) was not run: the assessment harness is auth-free by design, no credentials are present in the lab, and the REST path returns "Authentication needed". It would not have changed the verdict, because the fault is semantic, not syntactic.
authorize.conf\trole_user, role_power\ts.vendor_says: "A list of indexes that this role is allowed to search." Semicolon-separated list of index names; "Follows the same wildcarding semantics as the 'srchIndexesDefault' setting", where "*" does not match internal indexes and "_*" represents all internal indexes. No default. The setting has no TLS vocabulary of any kind.

authorize.conf\ttokens_auth\texpiration.live_evidence: btool authorize list --debug: [tokens_auth] expiration = +30d and ephemeralExpiration = +1h, both from /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/authorize.conf, with disabled = false. The assessment observations record expiration as found=present, value +30d. The instance settles the documentation's self-contradiction in favor of +30d, so not_equals never passes out of the box.
authorize.conf\ttokens_auth\texpiration.notes: "never" is in the accepted vocabulary, selecting it does create a token that is never invalidated, and forbidding it is a correct condition - so the criterion stands. It is not what makes this requirement Open: the assessment recorded server.conf [general] invalidateSessionTokensOnLogout = false and web.conf tools.sessions.restart_persist = True, and the expiration condition passed. Secondary observation for the record: an authorization token is a bearer credential, not a web session identifier, so this setting is adjacent to the requirement's "invalidate session identifiers upon logout" rather than on it; the server.conf and web.conf conditions in the same rule carry the actual objective.
authorize.conf\ttokens_auth\texpiration.vendor_says: expiration = <relative-time-modifier>|never. "The relative time when an authorization token expires." "Your account must hold the admin role to update this setting." The entry then states both "The default value indicates that a token never expires. To set token expiration, you must set this value to a relative time value." and "Default: +30d". The Splunk Enterprise token pages resolve it the other way from the first sentence: if no expiration is set the platform applies a global default of 30 days from issuance. ephemeralExpiration is separate and "cannot be given an expiration of "never"".

indexes.conf\t<index>\tcoldToFrozenDir.correction: indexes.conf [_audit] coldToFrozenDir non_empty  (with indexes.conf [_audit] coldToFrozenScript non_empty as the documented equivalent, and the stanza named literally for each index holding audit records)
indexes.conf\t<index>\tcoldToFrozenDir.live_evidence: /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/indexes.conf declares the key empty at lines 54-55: `coldToFrozenScript =` and `coldToFrozenDir =`. btool indexes list --debug shows `coldToFrozenDir = ` present with an empty value in all 19 index stanzas, and the evidence map records _audit coldToFrozenDir with an empty value field. evaluate.sh's operator returns true on key existence alone (`if (op == "present") return (found == "present")`), so the condition passes on a stock install that archives nothing. Separately, a throwaway btool tree accepted coldToFrozenDir = volume:probe_vol/frozen with btool check exit 0, although the 10.4.2 spec says a volume reference may not be used.
indexes.conf\t<index>\tcoldToFrozenDir.notes: This is the clearest defect in the file and it is only visible by reading the instance. The criterion's rationale is right - without an archive destination the vendor states frozen data is deleted - but `present` tests the wrong thing. The product ships the key declared and empty, so the condition is satisfied by exactly the configuration it was written to catch: no archive destination at all, data deleted at freeze. non_empty is the operator the rationale describes. Two cautions on the correction: evaluate.sh's wildcard() returns `any` for non_empty, so a placeholder stanza would be satisfied by one archived index out of nineteen - hence naming the audit index literally; and because the collector breaks on the first matching key, a placeholder or empty stanza is decided from _audit alone regardless. Note also that nothing in the collection path enforces the spec's prohibition on a volume reference here, so a configuration that satisfies the corrected condition can still carry a value splunkd will not use.
indexes.conf\t<index>\tcoldToFrozenDir.vendor_says: The 10.4 indexes.conf reference and the 10.4.2 spec shipped with the product (line 892) agree: "An alternative to a 'coldToFrozen' script - this setting lets you specify a destination path for the frozen archive"; "Splunk software automatically puts frozen buckets in this directory"; "If both 'coldToFrozenDir' and 'coldToFrozenScript' are specified, 'coldToFrozenDir' takes precedence"; "May NOT contain a volume reference"; and the block carries no Default line. Vendor 10.4 "Set a retirement and archiving policy": "The indexer deletes frozen data by default, but you can also archive it" and "If you want to archive frozen data instead of deleting it entirely, you must tell the indexer to do so."

indexes.conf\t<index>\tfrozenTimePeriodI.correction: Remove the condition and leave retention in external_dependencies, where the rules already record it. If a decidable condition is required, the only one that distinguishes anything is indexes.conf [_audit] frozenTimePeriodInSecs not_equals 188697600, which detects an untouched default - and even that produces a false finding where a site deliberately chooses six years.
indexes.conf\t<index>\tfrozenTimePeriodI.live_evidence: btool indexes list shows frozenTimePeriodInSecs present with a non-empty value in all 19 index stanzas, every one from /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/indexes.conf (188697600 for _audit, main, default, splunklogger, summary; 2592000 for _internal; 604800 for epo_all and history; and so on). Running the project's own assess/bin/evaluate.sh over the latest results, this condition is not among the failing conditions for any of the four requirements that use it.
indexes.conf\t<index>\tfrozenTimePeriodI.notes: The setting exists, the rationale is accurate, but the operator makes the condition vacuous: the product declares the key with a value in every index stanza of system/default, so `present` can never fail on any Splunk installation. The criterion therefore cannot distinguish a site that set a retention period from one that touched nothing, which is precisely what its own rationale says it is for. This is the default-already-satisfies case. The four findings it sits behind are all Open for unrelated conditions - savedsearches.conf dispatch times for SRG-APP-000368 and SRG-APP-000775, outputs.conf [tcpout] server for SRG-APP-000515, and for SRG-APP-000760 a malformed condition, `props.conf [<source type>] present`, which the parser reads as a key literally named "present". Secondary point worth carrying: vendor documentation states maxTotalDataSizeMB can freeze data before the period elapses, so this setting alone does not bound how far back a report or reduction can reach.
indexes.conf\t<index>\tfrozenTimePeriodI.vendor_says: Vendor 10.4 "Set a retirement and archiving policy": "This attribute specifies the number of seconds to elapse before data gets frozen" and "The default value is 188697600 seconds, or approximately 6 years." It also warns "If maxTotalDataSizeMB is reached before frozenTimePeriodInSecs, data will be rolled to frozen before the configured time period has elapsed." The 10.4 indexes.conf reference: nonnegative integer, highest legal value 4294967295, "Default: 188697600 (6 years)"; and "If you do not specify a coldToFrozenScript, data is deleted when rolled to frozen."

indexes.conf\t<index> / <index name>\ten.correction: indexes.conf [_audit] enableDataIntegrityControl in 1|true  (stanza made literal; setting, operator and operand unchanged)
indexes.conf\t<index> / <index name>\ten.live_evidence: podman exec -u splunk epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool indexes list --debug: enableDataIntegrityControl = false in all 19 index stanzas, every one sourced from /opt/splunk/etc/system/default/indexes.conf. Effect confirmed: splunk check-integrity -index _audit -verbose returned "Integrity check error for bucket ... Reason=Journal has no hashes." for both buckets, "Total buckets checked=2, succeeded=0, failed=2". Operand acceptance by splunkd not provable without a restart; in a throwaway btool tree (btool --dir, outside etc/) the values 1, True and yes were all read back verbatim and btool check exited 0 even for yes, which is not a Splunk boolean, so btool cannot be used to prove acceptance.
indexes.conf\t<index> / <index name>\ten.notes: The setting, the operator and the operand are right, the rationale matches what the setting does, and the finding is true: the instance computes no rawdata hashes, proven by check-integrity rather than inferred. The evaluator's `in` lowercases both sides, so the product STIG fix text wording "1 or True" also matches. Two addressing problems sit behind an otherwise sound criterion. First, the stanza is a placeholder: the collector compares stanzas literally (assess/bin/assess.sh, `if (stanza != "" && F[1] != stanza) continue`), so <index> and <index name> never match a real stanza and the key is recorded absent; this condition is only rescued because two other requirements collect the same key with an empty stanza, which evaluate.sh's wildcard() can resolve. <index name> is doubly impossible - the 10.4.2 spec states index names consist only of numbers, lowercase letters, underscores and hyphens, so a stanza containing a space cannot exist. Second, the collector breaks on the first matching key, so the value recorded is _audit's and the other 18 indexes are never examined. Also: vendor documentation states this feature is unavailable on SmartStore indexes, so on a SmartStore index this condition and the remote.s3.encryption condition cannot both be met.
indexes.conf\t<index> / <index name>\ten.vendor_says: Vendor 10.4 "Manage data integrity": edit indexes.conf and set enableDataIntegrityControl=true for each index; "The default value for this setting for all indexes is false (off)"; Splunk "computes hashes on every slice of data using the SHA-256 algorithm"; "Splunk Enterprise supports data integrity control on local indexes only. There is no support on SmartStore indexes"; verified with ./splunk check-integrity -index [index name] [-verbose]. The 10.4 indexes.conf reference gives the same block: boolean, "Default: false". The product's own 10.4.2 indexes.conf.spec, line 671, states Default: false.
