And 10.4.2 cross-references '[kvstore]:sslCRLPath' as the instance-wide CRL path guidance, which the assessment already reflects.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tcertificateStatu.vendor_says: Under [sslConfig], 'Default: empty string (certificate status validation checks are off)' and the only documented value is crl. The 10.4.2 spec text: 'Currently, the only acceptable value for this setting is "crl".' 'If you do not give this setting a value of "crl", the setting, and thus certificate status validation checks, are turned off.' 'When certificate status validation is active, it is active for any kind of Splunk platform-related network communication that uses SSL, including the Splunk Web, splunkd, and Splunk-to-Splunk (S2S) communication channels.' 'The default path for CRL files in a Splunk platform instance is at $SPLUNK_HOME/auth/crl. Any CRL files must reside there, and must be in privacy-enhanced mail (PEM) format.'

server.conf\tsslConfig\tcipherSuite.correction: Remove the three non_empty conditions on server.conf [sslConfig] cipherSuite; the value test under SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000188 is the only one that can carry a verdict.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tcipherSuite.live_evidence: btool server list sslConfig --debug resolves cipherSuite from '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf' on an instance with nothing local set for it. The assessment's harness reads the merged configuration - proven by its own observed values, for example 'server.conf [httpServer] acceptFrom not_equals * -> is *' where acceptFrom exists only in the default file - so non_empty on this key resolves true on every instance.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tcipherSuite.notes: non_empty cannot fail against a key the vendor ships a default for. The stated intent - that the approved cipher string be expressed by the application rather than inherited from the library - is reasonable, but the operator cannot see the difference, because the merged configuration shows the default as a value. The rationale is also factually behind 10.4.2: it says an unset value falls back to 'whatever cipher string the OpenSSL binary provides', whereas 10.4.2 ships an explicit list in the default file.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tcipherSuite.vendor_says: cipherSuite has no fixed default: 'The default can vary. See the cipherSuite setting in the $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf file for the current default.' It is not an empty-by-default setting - the vendor ships a value.

server.conf\tsslConfig\tecdhCurves.live_evidence: Vendor-prescribed check run on the instance: 'splunk cmd openssl ecparam -list_curves' lists prime256v1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 as present, so all three operands are valid named curves on this build. btool shows the live value is '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf ecdhCurves = prime256v1, secp384r1, secp521r1' - the criterion's exact list is already the vendor default. The [tls1.3] stanza ships 'groups = prime256v1, secp384r1, secp521r1' separately.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tecdhCurves.notes: The operands are valid and the criterion is satisfied by the shipped default, so neither of its two conditions can contribute to a finding on a 10.4.2 instance; SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000188 is Open on its cipherSuite sibling, not on this. Two cautions worth recording. The exact-list pin rejects a reordering and rejects the FIPS 140-3 subset, and the vendor states secp521r1 is not FIPS 140-3 approved while other conditions in this assessment require FIPS mode - the criterion and the FIPS conditions pull against each other. And ecdhCurves governs TLS 1.2 only; the TLS 1.3 equivalent is [tls1.3] groups, which no condition covers.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tecdhCurves.vendor_says: 'The ecdhCurves setting in [sslConfig] controls key exchange curves for TLS 1.2 connections.' Example value: 'ecdhCurves = prime256v1, secp384r1, secp521r1'. 'For TLS 1.3 connections, the equivalent setting is groups in the [tls1.3] stanza.' FIPS: 'Only AES-GCM cipher suites and the secp384r1 and secp256r1 curves are FIPS 140-3 approved.' The 10.4.2 spec adds 'The server supports only the curves specified in the list' and prescribes the verification command: 'splunk cmd openssl ecparam -list_curves'.

server.conf\tsslConfig\tenableSplunkdSSL.live_evidence: btool server list sslConfig --debug: '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf enableSplunkdSSL = true' - the shipped default is already true. Confirmed in practice: the management port completes a TLS 1.2 handshake ('New, TLSv1.2, Cipher is ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384'), and splunkd.log records 'loader [HTTPDispatch] - Server supporting SSL versions=TLS1.2'.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tenableSplunkdSSL.notes: Sound and satisfied by the shipped default on 10.4.2, verified both from configuration and from a live handshake, so none of the five conditions on this key can carry a finding by itself. Both operand spellings, in 1|true and in true|1, are equivalent and both accept the live value.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tenableSplunkdSSL.vendor_says: The vendor's own [sslConfig] example for TLS 1.2 and 1.3 opens with 'enableSplunkdSSL = true', and the 10.4 server.conf reference documents it as the switch for TLS on the splunkd management and KV Store ports.

server.conf\tsslConfig\trequireClientCer.live_evidence: The key is in the 10.4.2 spec at line 895 under [sslConfig] (header at line 744), and separately under [replication_port-ssl://<port>] at lines 4398 and 5441, which cross-reference the [sslConfig] description. It has no entry in the shipped default file and no line in btool server list sslConfig --debug, so the documented default of false applies.
server.conf\tsslConfig\trequireClientCer.notes: Sound against 10.4.2. The key exists in the stanza named, the default is false, and the rationale matches the vendor's description of what true demands. Scope note rather than a defect: this governs clients connecting to the splunkd management and REST listener and the inter-instance channels, not the Splunk Web interface that SRG-APP-000427-WSR-000186 is worded for - that is web.conf requireClientCert, which the finding's other conditions already cover. Treating the splunkd listener as the second interface subject to the same requirement is the right reading.
server.conf\tsslConfig\trequireClientCer.vendor_says: 'requireClientCert = <boolean>', 'Default: false'. 'Whether or not an HTTPS client which connects to a splunkd server must possess a certificate that a certificate authority signed to complete the connection.' 'Splunk platform indexers must use this setting to connect to other Splunk platform indexers. Deployment clients must present certificates to deployment servers before they can poll the servers for new configurations or applications.' 'A value of "false" means that there is no certificate requirement to connect to services on another Splunk platform instance.' The vendor's inter-Splunk [sslConfig] example includes 'requireClientCert = true'.

server.conf\tsslConfig\tserverCert.live_evidence: The shipped default file writes the unexpanded token: line 173, 'serverCert = $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/server.pem'. btool does not expand $SPLUNK_HOME - the same output shows '[app_backup] backup_path = $SPLUNK_HOME/var/backup' unexpanded - so a literal comparison against '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/server.pem' does match an instance left on the auto-generated certificate. On this instance a real certificate is set locally, so the condition passes.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tserverCert.notes: The not_equals condition under SRG-APP-000915-AU-000400 is sound, and the literal form of the operand works because btool reports the token unexpanded rather than as an absolute path - a comparison against the expanded form would have been a false negative. Narrow limit: it detects only the auto-generated default path, not a self-signed certificate placed at a different path, so it is necessary rather than sufficient for the requirement.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tserverCert.vendor_says: 'Default: $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/server.pem'. 'The Splunk daemon auto-generates certificates when you start Splunk Enterprise the first time.' 'Where applicable, replace the default certificate with a certificate that you either create on your own or obtain from a third party.'

server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslPassword.live_evidence: The shipped default file writes the literal default at line 174: 'sslPassword = password'. On this instance btool resolves the local value to the product's encrypted form, '$7$' followed by base64 - so the criterion's ^\$ test does separate an encrypted value from the shipped plaintext default. The key is in the 10.4.2 spec at line 1026 under [sslConfig].
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslPassword.notes: Sound: the key exists, the default is the published literal 'password', and ^\$ distinguishes the product's encrypted form from it. One limit of the test that the requirement wording invites but the operator cannot deliver: splunkd rewrites any plaintext sslPassword into the $7$ form on startup, so an operator who typed a weak password - including the word 'password' itself, written explicitly - will present an encrypted value and satisfy the condition. The criterion tests the storage form, not the strength or custody of the key material, and the hardware-protected key store that SRG-APP-000915-AU-000400 asks about is not expressible in server.conf at all and belongs in external_dependencies.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslPassword.vendor_says: 'sslPassword = <string>', 'The password for the server certificate, if you created one.' 'Default: password'. The deprecated predecessor sslKeysfilePassword is documented as superseded by it.

server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslRootCAPath.live_evidence: No entry for sslRootCAPath in the shipped default file, so the merged configuration shows a value only when one is written - non_empty is falsifiable here, unlike on the defaulted keys. On this instance btool resolves it from '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/local/server.conf sslRootCAPath = <labcerts>/ca.pem', a local setting.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslRootCAPath.notes: Sound in every respect checked: the key exists under [sslConfig] in 10.4.2, it has no default, and non_empty is therefore a real test rather than a vacuous one. The companion claim that Splunk Web falls back to this value is a web.conf question and outside this file's scope, but it is why writing the condition against server.conf rather than web.conf is the right call. One limit worth stating: a path being set says nothing about which anchors the file holds, so the 'only approved trust anchors' part of SRG-APP-000910 is only partly reachable from configuration.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslRootCAPath.vendor_says: 'The path to the certificate authority (CA), or root certificate store.' 'The certificate store must be a file that contains one or more CA certificates that have been concatenated together. This setting expects a value that represents a file object, not a directory object.' 'If you run Splunk Enterprise in Common Criteria mode, then you must give this setting a value.' The 10.4 reference lists no default for it.

server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVerifyServerC.live_evidence: The key is in the 10.4.2 spec at line 835 under [sslConfig]. It has no entry in the shipped default file, and btool server list sslConfig --debug shows no sslVerifyServerCert line, so the documented default of false applies and the assessment's observed 'not set' is accurate. btool does show other stanzas carrying their own copies - [applicationsManagement] true, [kvstore] false, [distributed_leases] false, [pythonSslClientConfig] false - which confirms the per-stanza structure the criterion relies on.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVerifyServerC.notes: Sound: key, stanza, operand and rationale all match 10.4.2, and the default is false, so the conditions under SRG-APP-000427-AU-000040 and SRG-APP-000910-AU-000390 are real. Both operand spellings, equals true and in 1|true, accept the same values. One observation from the instance: the local file sets sslVerifyServerName = true while sslVerifyServerCert is unset, and the vendor states 'For this setting to have any effect, the sslVerifyServerCert setting must have a value of "true"' - so the host name check configured here is currently inert, which the splunkd CLI itself warns about at every invocation.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVerifyServerC.vendor_says: 'sslVerifyServerCert = <boolean>', 'Default: false'. 'Whether or not splunkd, as a client, validates the TLS certificate that a server presents to it when it connects to a server.' 'A value of "true" means that the client inspects and validates the certificate that it receives from the server upon connecting to it... The client then checks both the X.509 Common Name and Subject Alternative Name of the server in the certificate for a match.' 'A value of "false" means that the client does not check the TLS certificate that it receives as part of the session negotiation. The client considers any valid TLS certificate as acceptable.'

server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersions.correction: server.conf [sslConfig] sslVersions matches ^[[:space:]]*(tls1\.2|tls1\.3)([[:space:]]*,[[:space:]]*(tls1\.2|tls1\.3))*[[:space:]]*$   AND a new condition  server.conf [sslConfig] deprecatedTlsVersionSupport in false|0
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersions.live_evidence: Shipped default file line 163: 'sslVersions = tls1.2, tls1.3'. The hardening app overrides it in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/local/server.conf with 'sslVersions = tls1.2'. Measured against the live management port with the product's own OpenSSL 3.5.7 (splunk cmd openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8089): -tls1 rejected (protocol version alert), -tls1_1 rejected, -tls1_2 accepted as ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, -tls1_3 REJECTED. splunkd.log: 'loader [HTTPDispatch] - Server supporting SSL versions=TLS1.2' for splunkd and 'UiHttpListener - Server supporting SSL versions=TLS1.2,TLS1.3' for Splunk Web. So sslVersions does gate TLS 1.3 on this listener, and the local override has removed TLS 1.3 from it.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersions.notes: Four separate operand defects. (1) No operand admits tls1.3: the regex alternation is (tls1.2|*|tls) with exclusion branches only for ssl2/ssl3/tls1.0/tls1.1, and 'equals tls1.2' is exact, so both reject the vendor default 'tls1.2, tls1.3' and reject tls1.3-only - configurations strictly stronger than the one the criteria demand. (2) The ssl3 exclusions are dead: SSLv3 support was removed in 10.4.0 and the spec says -ssl3 'has no effect'. (3) The tls1.0 and tls1.1 exclusions are unreachable: deprecatedTlsVersionSupport defaults to false and the instance logs that those versions 'are not available for configuration'. (4) 'not_in *|tls' and 'not_in ssl3|tls1.0|tls1.1|tls|*' remain defensible in intent, but on 10.4.0 and higher 'tls' includes TLS 1.3, so the rationale given for them no longer describes what the value selects. Separately, the SRG-APP-000383-WSR-000175 condition uses non_empty, which cannot fail: the merged configuration always resolves a shipped default, so the operator cannot distinguish a declared list from an inherited one, which is exactly what its rationale asks for.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersions.vendor_says: 'Version 1.3 of the TLS protocol is available starting in Splunk Enterprise version 10.4.0' and is 'Active alongside TLS 1.2 by default when you upgrade to version 10.4.0 or higher'. TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are 'Turned off by default'. SSLv3 is 'Not supported' with 'Support removed in version 10.4.0'. 'At version 10.4.0 and higher, sslVersions = "tls" includes TLS 1.3.' The inter-Splunk page states 'Supported values are "tls1.2" and "tls1.3"' and 'The default at version 10.4.0 and higher is tls1.2,tls1.3.' The 10.4.2 spec adds: 'The versions available are "tls1.0", "tls1.1", "tls1.2", and "tls1.3"' and '"-ssl2" and "-ssl3" are accepted as values in the version list, but have no effect.'

server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersionsForCl.live_evidence: btool server list sslConfig --debug: '$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/server.conf sslVersionsForClient = tls1.2, tls1.3'. Confirmed by reading the shipped file itself, line 164. Nothing local overrides it. The value is the untouched vendor default.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersionsForCl.notes: This is the verdict-altering one. The live value is the vendor default 'tls1.2, tls1.3'. 'equals tls1.2' fails it, and the regex ^\s*(tls1\.2|\*|tls)(\s*,\s*-(ssl2|ssl3|tls1\.0|tls1\.1))*\s*$ fails it as well because the pattern has no tls1.3 branch. For SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000156 the two server.conf conditions are sslVersions (which passes on this instance) and sslVersionsForClient (which fails), so that finding is Open solely because the product ships TLS 1.3 alongside TLS 1.2. The configuration is not deficient; the criterion is. Meeting the criterion as written would require writing sslVersionsForClient = tls1.2, which removes TLS 1.3 from splunkd's outgoing connections and weakens the instance.
server.conf\tsslConfig\tsslVersionsForCl.vendor_says: 'The default at version 10.4.0 and higher is tls1.2,tls1.3.' The 10.4.2 spec: 'The list of TLS/SSL versions to support for outgoing HTTP connections from splunkd. This includes distributed search, deployment client, etc.' and 'The syntax is the same as the sslVersions setting.' The 10.4 server.conf reference gives no fixed default and directs the reader to the shipped default file.

splunk-launch.conf\t\tOPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_F.correction: splunk-launch.conf [] OPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_FILE_LOCKING not_equals 1, evaluated against the vendor-documented default of 0 when the setting is absent, which yields Not a Finding on this instance.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tOPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_F.live_evidence: The setting is in the 10.4.2 shipped spec at lines 226-233 and is absent from /opt/splunk/etc/splunk-launch.conf and from `splunk envvars`, so the effective value on this instance is the documented default, 0, which already satisfies the condition. The literal OPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_FILE_LOCKING is present in /opt/splunk/bin/splunkd, near the lock-file strings, so splunkd does read it. Vocabulary probe by the throwaway-environment method accepted 1, 0, true, false and banana at rc=0, so the launcher applies no pre-flight validation here and the probe could not establish the accepted vocabulary; the lock check itself runs at startup, and testing it would need a restart, which is out of bounds.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tOPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_F.notes: The condition itself is well formed and the rationale is faithful to the vendor text, including the quoted caution. What is wrong is the verdict. This is a negative condition over a setting whose documented default already complies, so an absent setting is the compliant state, and recording Open because the setting is "not set" inverts the test. Any other `not_equals` condition in this file carries the same hazard and should be checked for it. One citation error to fix while this finding is reopened: the shipped specification cites splunk-launch.conf.spec:214-220 for this setting, but in the 10.4.2 spec that range is the caution prose and the setting is at 226-233. The SPLUNK_FIPS citation at line 110 is exact, so the specification is keyed to the right spec file and this one reference is simply wrong.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tOPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_F.vendor_says: "OPTIMISTIC_ABOUT_FILE_LOCKING = [0|1]", "Whether or not Splunk software skips the file system lock check on unrecognized file systems." "CAUTION: USE THIS SETTING AT YOUR OWN RISK. YOU CAN LOSE ANY DATA THAT HAS BEEN INDEXED WHILE THE SETTING IS ACTIVE." "When set to 1, Splunk software skips the file system check, and splunkd starts whether or not it can recognize the file system." "Defaults to 0 (Run the file system check.)" The surrounding caution block in the 10.4.2 shipped spec adds that use of the setting is not supported and that irrevocable data loss can occur.

splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_BINDIP.correction: Keep splunk-launch.conf [] SPLUNK_BINDIP non_empty and add splunk-launch.conf [] SPLUNK_BINDIP not_in 0.0.0.0|::|*
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_BINDIP.live_evidence: Not set in /opt/splunk/etc/splunk-launch.conf and absent from `splunk envvars`, so the Open finding is factually correct. Vocabulary probe by the same throwaway-environment method accepted every value at rc=0, including 10.0.0.5, 0.0.0.0, ::, the literal string not-an-ip, and 999.999.999.999. The launcher therefore enforces nothing against the documented <ip address> vocabulary, and the criterion's `non_empty` operator is satisfied by values that confine nothing at all.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_BINDIP.notes: The rationale is sound and is confirmed by the vendor text: splunkd's management port and its forwarder-receiving ports are both bound by this setting, so Splunk Web's server.socket_host does not cover them and a second condition on this file is justified. The defect is that `non_empty` admits 0.0.0.0 and ::, the exact unspecified addresses the companion web.conf condition on the same finding already rejects with `not_in 0.0.0.0|::`. The two conditions in one finding are inconsistent in strictness, and an instance set to SPLUNK_BINDIP=0.0.0.0 would clear this condition while leaving every listener on every interface. The live probe shows the product will not catch that for the assessor, since it validates nothing. Two further points for the write-up rather than the condition: the vendor's own spec says a firewall is typically the superior restriction, which is an external_dependencies observation, not grounds to drop the condition; and the spec contradicts itself on Splunk Web, claiming at line 80 that splunkweb binds to this address and at lines 93-94 that it does not override server.socket_host for Splunk Web.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_BINDIP.vendor_says: "SPLUNK_BINDIP = <ip address>", "The network IP address that splunkd and splunkweb should bind to, as opposed to binding to the default for the local operating system." Default: not set, in which case the platform "effectively binds to '*', meaning an unspecified bind". "For splunkd, this sets both the management port and the ports that receive from forwarders." "NOTE: When using this setting you must update 'mgmtHostPort' in web.conf to match." The shipped 10.4.2 spec adds at lines 90-94 that the setting is useful "either to enable or restrict access. But using a firewall is typically a superior method of restriction", and that it "Does not override web.conf/[settings]/server.socket_host for SplunkWeb if set; the latter is preferred when SplunkWeb behavior is the focus."

splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_COMMON_CRIT.correction: Remove the condition. The requirement's cryptographic-module objective is already carried by the SPLUNK_FIPS condition on the same finding.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_COMMON_CRIT.live_evidence: The literal SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA is present in both /opt/splunk/bin/splunkd and /opt/splunk/bin/splunk on the 10.4.2 instance, in splunkd's string table immediately beside SPLUNK_FIPS and /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled, so splunkd reads it. It is not set in /opt/splunk/etc/splunk-launch.conf and does not appear in `splunk envvars`. Vocabulary probe via the same throwaway-environment method: 1, 0, true, false and banana were all accepted at rc=0, so the launcher applies no pre-flight validation to it, in contrast to SPLUNK_FIPS which aborts on a bad value. Whether the value takes effect cannot be shown without a restart, which is out of bounds, so the vocabulary and activation remain untested. The cited fix text was confirmed against the local benchmark: SPLK-CL-000390 in U_Splunk_Enterprise_8-x_for_Linux_STIG_V2R3 does literally prescribe "SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA=1 SPLUNK_FIPS=1", so the assessor quoted it accurately.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_COMMON_CRIT.notes: The setting exists in 10.4.2, so this is not a phantom key, but the criterion assumes it selects compliant cryptographic modules. The only vendor description of its effect, in the product's own server.conf.spec, is that it makes splunkd consult the CRL file; Common Criteria mode is an evaluated-configuration mode, not a cryptographic-module selector, and the FIPS objective is met by SPLUNK_FIPS. Three further reasons this should not stand as a condition: the vendor does not document the setting in the file reference where an operator would configure it, so no operator can be held to it; there is no 10.x Common Criteria manual or published 10.x target of evaluation, and the vendor's 9.2 manual restricts the mode to a single instance on a single machine with no support for distributed deployments, which an indexer in this deployment is not; and the launcher validates nothing, so a typo silently leaves the mode off while the configuration file reads as compliant. If the program genuinely requires the NIAP evaluated configuration, that is an external_dependencies item, because the certified configuration is a product-version and deployment-topology fact rather than something this application's configuration establishes. Note also that the fix text relied on comes from the Splunk Enterprise 8.x STIG, two major versions behind the system under assessment.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_COMMON_CRIT.vendor_says: No vendor documentation defines this setting. It is absent from the 10.4 splunk-launch.conf reference and from the 10.0, 9.2, 9.1 and 9.0 editions of the same page, and absent from the 10.4 FIPS guide and the 10.4 "Best practice for maintaining compliance with FIPS and Common Criteria" page. The only vendor text naming it is the specification shipped inside 10.4.2 itself, server.conf.spec:5646-5648, which says splunkd uses the CRL file "When the Splunk platform instance is in Common Criteria mode (SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA=1)". The 10.4.2 splunk-launch.conf.spec:60-64 points the operator to a "Securing Splunk Enterprise for Common Criteria" manual for the certification status; no 10.x edition of that manual exists, and the vendor's 10.4 best-practice page links the 9.2 edition. Splunk-launch.conf does accept undeclared variables: splunk-launch.conf.spec:33-36 states "<environment_variable>=<value>" and "Any desired environment variable can be set to any value."

splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_DB.correction: Delete all four conditions: splunk-launch.conf [] SPLUNK_DB matches tls1\.2, and splunk-launch.conf [] SPLUNK_DB not_matches (^|,)[[:space:]]*ssl3 / tls1\.0 / tls1\.1. The TLS version tests belong on web.conf [settings] sslVersions and server.conf [sslConfig] sslVersions and sslVersionsForClient, under the requirements that concern transport encryption.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_DB.live_evidence: The four conditions apply TLS version-list regexes to the index-path setting: `matches tls1\.2`, and `not_matches (^|,)[[:space:]]*ssl3`, `...tls1\.0`, `...tls1\.1`. On the 10.4.2 instance SPLUNK_DB is consumed only as the index-path root, shown by `btool indexes list main --debug` resolving homePath and coldPath from $SPLUNK_DB, and by `splunk envvars` reporting it as a directory path. The throwaway-environment probe accepted SPLUNK_DB=tls1.2 at rc=0, which is the only way the `matches tls1\.2` condition could ever be cleared: by setting the index root to a path literally containing the string tls1.2. The three not_matches conditions are vacuously true for any directory path and can never fail. The contamination is also visible in the shipped specification itself, where the rationale for the matches condition is spliced and truncated mid-sentence: "the version list must offer TLS 1.2 (fix text directs placing the document directories \"in a separate partition from the web se)".
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_DB.notes: This covers conditions two through five on this setting. These are TLS criteria copied onto a filesystem path setting, the same class of defect as the earlier round's key named role_<roleName>. Two of the consequences matter for the finding: `matches tls1\.2` is unsatisfiable by any legitimate value, so SRG-APP-000233-WSR-000146 can never be cleared no matter what the operator does, and the three negative conditions can never fail, so they add nothing but noise to the finding's evidence. All five SPLUNK_DB conditions share the one srg_id, so removing these four and correcting the non_empty condition rewrites that finding in full. The spliced rationale text is worth keeping in the record, because it shows the contamination happened when the condition was generated rather than when it was evaluated.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_DB.vendor_says: The vendor documents SPLUNK_DB solely as the fully qualified path to the directory containing index directories, used by paths expressed in indexes.conf. No vendor text associates it with TLS, SSL, protocol versions or cipher selection. TLS version lists in this product are sslVersions in web.conf and server.conf and sslVersionsForClient in server.conf, which are different settings in different files.

splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_FIPS.live_evidence: Instance confirmed as Splunk 10.4.2 (build 33c3bf42cd73). The setting is absent from /opt/splunk/etc/splunk-launch.conf and absent from `splunk envvars` output; splunkd.log carries zero FIPS lines; /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled does not exist on the host or in the container, so the vendor's kernel-FIPS auto-enable path does not apply and the Open finding is factually correct on this instance. Vocabulary tested by injecting the variable into the environment of a throwaway read-only process (`podman exec -u splunk -e SPLUNK_FIPS=<v> epo-uat-indexer /opt/splunk/bin/splunk btool check`), which writes nothing and does not restart the instance. Accepted at rc=0: 1, 0, true, false, True, False, TRUE, FALSE, yes, no, t, f, YES, T. Rejected at rc=1 with "SPLUNK_FIPS setting has been set to a bad value '<v>', cannot continue!": 2, -1, 140-3, on, off, y, n, enabled, disabled. So the implemented vocabulary is Splunk's case-insensitive boolean set {0,1,true,false,t,f,yes,no}, not the [0|1] the documentation declares. With SPLUNK_FIPS=1 set, SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION accepted 140-2 and 140-3 and aborted on 140-4 and banana with "SPLUNK_FIPS is turned on, but SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION is configured with an invalid value in splunk-launch.conf." The splunkd binary also carries the strings "Failed to enable FIPS support: OPENSSL_CONF is not set", "Can't enable FIPS support: SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION is invalid or SPLUNK_FIPS is not set." and "FIPS provider enabled. provider: ", and the literals SPLUNK_FIPS, /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled and SPLUNK_COMMON_CRITERIA sit adjacent in its string table. `splunk show fips-mode` and /services/server/info both require authentication, which I did not have, so the runtime state was established from the file, envvars, the log and the kernel rather than from the vendor's own verification command.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_FIPS.notes: The setting is real, is the right setting for every requirement that cites it, and the Open verdict is correct on this instance. The defect is the operand. Twelve of the fourteen conditions test `equals 1`; SRG-APP-000014-WSR-000006 tests `in 1|true`; SRG-APP-000610-AU-000050 tests `in 1|true|True|TRUE`. The live vocabulary probe shows a production instance configured as SPLUNK_FIPS=true, SPLUNK_FIPS=T or SPLUNK_FIPS=yes is accepted by the product, and the vendor's own spec prose at splunk-launch.conf.spec:119-128 tells the operator to configure it to "true". Any `equals 1` test therefore scores a genuinely FIPS-enabled instance as a finding. SRG-APP-000610-AU-000050 is the closest of the three and still misses t/T/yes/YES. Two caveats I could not close: acceptance by the launcher's pre-flight validator is not proof that a value activates FIPS, because that needs a restart, which is out of bounds here; and the vendor states FIPS mode works only if the host operating system also runs in FIPS mode, which is an external dependency, not an application setting, so the condition carries only the application's share. Separately, the rationale behind SRG-APP-000224-WSR-000135, -000136 and -000139 asserts that FIPS mode is the application's only control over the random source used for Splunk Web session identifiers. No vendor documentation I could find supports that; Splunk Web session identifiers are issued by the Python web layer, not the OpenSSL FIPS provider the splunkd strings reference, so that specific rationale is an inference and should be marked undetermined rather than stated as fact. One more unstated prerequisite: splunkd refuses FIPS when OPENSSL_CONF is unset, and this instance sets OPENSSL_CONF=/opt/splunk/share/openssl3/openssl.cnf. Finally, and outside the conditions in scope: this instance ships PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0 in splunk-launch.conf, which splunkd itself flags with "PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY is set to 0 in splunk-launch.conf disabling certificate validation", and no condition in the file covers it.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_FIPS.vendor_says: The 10.4 reference declares "SPLUNK_FIPS = [0|1]" with "Default: 0", states "NOTE: This setting is one-time only.", and that "If you configure it to "true" and then start the Splunk platform instance, you cannot later configure it to "false"." It also states the setting is "true" by default when the host kernel runs in FIPS mode, and pairs with SPLUNK_FIPS_VERSION = [140-2|140-3], default 140-2. The 10.4 FIPS guide (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/establish-and-maintain-compliance-with-fips-and-common-criteria-in-splunk-enterprise/secure-splunk-enterprise-with-fips) instructs the literal line "SPLUNK_FIPS=1" in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/splunk-launch.conf before first start, states "FIPS mode works only if the operating system on which you run Splunk Enterprise also runs in FIPS mode", and gives verification as "splunk show fips-mode" returning "FIPS mode enabled" or /services/server/info returning fips_mode=1.

splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_OS_USER.live_evidence: Probed with the throwaway-environment method: SPLUNK_OS_USER=root was refused with "Failed to run splunk as SPLUNK_OS_USER. This command can only be run by bootstart user." That refusal is contextual, not a product-wide prohibition. The invoking account in this probe is splunk, uid 333, which cannot setuid to root, so the launcher's gate fired on the invoking identity exactly as the generated conf comment describes. An instance whose service is started from a root login would accept root here and splunkd would then run as root, so the condition remains falsifiable and worth testing.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_OS_USER.notes: This covers the second of the two conditions on this setting, `not_equals root`. Setting, stanza, operator and operand all check out against both the vendor text and the instance, and the rationale matches what the setting does. Keep it as written. I record the rejection of root in my probe deliberately: it would be easy to read that result as proof the product forbids root and therefore the condition can never fail, and that reading would be wrong, because the refusal came from the launcher's gate on the invoking account rather than from any check on the operand.
splunk-launch.conf\t\tSPLUNK_OS_USER.vendor_says: As above. The setting names the OS user whose privileges splunkd adopts, so naming root directs splunkd to retain root privileges rather than drop them, which is the converse of the documented purpose.

web.conf\troot_endpoint\troot_endpoint.correction: Drop the [root_endpoint] condition. The containment control the requirement is asking about is already covered by web.conf [settings] static_dir present; if a URI-prefix condition is wanted it must read web.conf [settings] root_endpoint present, which the vendor default already satisfies.
web.conf\troot_endpoint\troot_endpoint.live_evidence: The only stanza headers in the 10.4.2 shipped spec are [settings], [remoteUI], [admin_config_ui], [smc], [endpoint:<python_module_name>], [expose:<unique_name>] and [nghttpx_server] - there is no [root_endpoint]. btool web list --debug shows root_endpoint = / under [settings], from etc/system/default/web.conf.
web.conf\troot_endpoint\troot_endpoint.notes: The stanza does not exist in web.conf, so the condition reads a value that can never be set and reports "not set" unconditionally - the same class of defect as the authorize.conf criterion written against the placeholder key role_<roleName>. Corrected to [settings], the condition passes on the vendor default. The rationale is also a misreading: root_endpoint is a URL namespace prefix for the appserver, not a filesystem document root, and it does not contain users to a directory tree. SRG-APP-000141-WSR-000087's other two web.conf conditions are also spurious (see tools.staticdir.generate_indexes); only the authorize.conf srchFilter condition remains.
web.conf\troot_endpoint\troot_endpoint.vendor_says: "root_endpoint = <URI_prefix_string>. Defines the root URI path on which the appserver will listen. For example, if you want to proxy the splunk UI at http://splunk:8000/splunkui, then set root_endpoint = /splunkui. Default: /" It is documented in [settings]; the vendor page documents no stanza named [root_endpoint].

web.conf\tsettings\tSSOMode.correction: Drop the condition, or make it conditional: require SSOMode not_equals permissive only where enableCertBasedUserAuth is not true, since the vendor requires permissive for CAC.
web.conf\tsettings\tSSOMode.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: SSOMode = strict from etc/system/default/web.conf - the value the reference page documents, not the 'lax' the shipped spec claims. The condition appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tSSOMode.notes: Three findings here. The condition is already satisfied by the vendor default, so it contributes nothing to SRG-APP-000223-WSR-000145, which is Open on remoteUserMatchExact alone. The 10.4.2 shipped spec documents a default ('lax') that is not in the setting's own value list - a vendor spec defect, contradicted by both the reference page and the shipped default file. And most consequentially, the condition is mutually unsatisfiable with the seven CAC conditions in this same scope: the vendor CAC page requires SSOMode = permissive, so an instance built to satisfy enableCertBasedUserAuth and requireClientCert must fail this condition. That conflict needs resolving before either set is published.
web.conf\tsettings\tSSOMode.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "SSOMode = [permissive | strict]... When set to 'permissive': Requests to Splunk Web that originate from an untrusted IP address are redirected to a login page where they can log into Splunk Web without using SSO. When set to 'strict': All requests to Splunk Web will be restricted to those originating from a trusted IP except those to endpoints that do not require authentication. Default: lax" - 'lax' is not one of its own two values. The vendor 10.4 web.conf page states the default is strict. The 10.4 CAC page states SSOMode "must use permissive" for CAC authentication, with trustedIP set to 127.0.0.1.

web.conf\tsettings\tacceptFrom.correction: Replace the non_empty condition with web.conf [settings] acceptFrom not_matches (^|[,[:space:]])\*([,[:space:]]|$) , and keep not_equals * as a weaker companion.
web.conf\tsettings\tacceptFrom.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: acceptFrom = * from etc/system/default/web.conf.
web.conf\tsettings\tacceptFrom.notes: The underlying finding is genuine - the default accepts from anywhere, and 'not_equals *' is what records it. But the 'non_empty' condition paired with it is met by the value '*' itself, so it can be satisfied while the server still accepts from everywhere; it adds nothing and would mask the gap if the stronger condition were ever dropped. The suggested not_matches also closes the case the vendor's own syntax allows, a list such as '10.1/16, *', which 'not_equals *' lets through.
web.conf\tsettings\tacceptFrom.vendor_says: "Lists a set of networks or addresses from which to accept connections. Separate multiple rules with commas or spaces." Rule forms are a single IPv4/IPv6 address, a CIDR block, a DNS name possibly with '*' as a wildcard, and "'*', which matches anything". "You can also prefix an entry with '!' to cause the rule to reject the connection. The input applies rules in order, and uses the first one that matches... Default: '*' (accept from anywhere)"

web.conf\tsettings\tallowSslCompression.correction: Drop the web.conf condition as inert for 10.4.2, or qualify it as applying only where TLS 1.3 is disabled. The cookie-compression objective on a TLS 1.3 listener is governed by HTTP-layer compression (enable_gzip), not by this setting.
web.conf\tsettings\tallowSslCompression.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: allowSslCompression = false from etc/system/default/web.conf (line 469), and enable_gzip = True. TLS 1.3 is enabled and live - the handshake probe negotiated TLSv1.3/TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 - so the setting is inert on this listener. The web.conf condition appears in no observed_reason; SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000153 is Open on the server.conf [sslConfig] instance of the same setting.
web.conf\tsettings\tallowSslCompression.notes: The setting exists and the operand is within its vocabulary, and the web.conf condition already passes on the default - so no finding is misreported here. The substantive point is that in 10.4.2 the vendor documents this setting as having no effect when TLS 1.3 is enabled, which is the default state. A criterion that cannot affect the objective on a stock 10.4.2 instance should not be carried as the control for it. This fact exists only in the 10.4.2 spec, not in the 10.0.0 file the assessment was built from, and it applies equally to the server.conf [sslConfig] condition that is actually recording SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000153 Open.
web.conf\tsettings\tallowSslCompression.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "Whether or not the server lets clients negotiate SSL-layer data compression... The HTTP layer has its own compression layer which is usually sufficient. In Splunk Enterprise version 10.4 and later, this setting has no effect when TLS 1.3 is enabled. TLS 1.3 does not support SSL-layer compression. To use compression for HTTPS connections with TLS 1.3, both the HTTP client and the server must enable HTTP-layer compression... Default: false". The 10.0.0 spec carries no TLS 1.3 statement. The vendor cipher page makes the same point for the related outputs.conf setting: it "has no effect for TLS 1.3 connections because TLS 1.3 does not support SSL compression".

web.conf\tsettings\tallowSsoWithoutChang.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: allowSsoWithoutChangingServerConf = 0 from etc/system/default/web.conf. The condition appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tallowSsoWithoutChang.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, so it does not contribute to the Open verdict. The condition is sound in direction and worth keeping as a guard, and it is consistent with the CAC requirement that trustedIP be set to 127.0.0.1 in server.conf.
web.conf\tsettings\tallowSsoWithoutChang.vendor_says: "Whether or not to allow SSO without setting the 'trustedIP' setting in server.conf as well as in web.conf. If set to 1, enables web-based SSO without a 'trustedIP' setting configured in server.conf. Default: 0"

web.conf\tsettings\tappServerProcessLogS.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: appServerProcessLogStderr = false from etc/system/default/web.conf (lowercase in the vendor's file). Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tappServerProcessLogS.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, so it contributes nothing to either finding. The rationale is accurate and quotes the spec correctly, including the session-ID disclosure risk, so the condition is worth keeping as a guard. Worth noting the destination is splunkd.log, an on-disk internal log, not the client - so the exposure is to anyone who can read internal indexes rather than to a remote user, which is a different control surface from the other SRG-APP-000266 conditions.
web.conf\tsettings\tappServerProcessLogS.vendor_says: "If set to true, messages written to the standard error stream by the Python-based application server processes will be logged to splunkd.log under the 'UiAppServer' channel. This can be useful when debugging issues when the appserver process fails to start. However, some appserver code may print sensitive information such as session ID strings to standard error so this defaults to disabled. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthMet.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; absent from the shipped default web.conf and from btool output, matching the spec's "No default". Operand acceptance untested (expired CLI session, as above), but the three operand tokens are quoted verbatim from both the spec and the vendor CAC page.
web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthMet.notes: Setting, stanza, vocabulary and absence of a default all check out against both the shipped spec and the vendor CAC page, and the finding is genuine on this instance. The 'non_empty' variant under SRG-APP-000150-AU-002320 and the 'in CommonName|EDIPI|PIV' variant elsewhere are consistent with each other. Which of the three methods a site picks is an organization decision, so testing membership rather than a specific value is the right shape. Carries the same SSOMode and LDAP dependencies as enableCertBasedUserAuth.
web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthMet.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "The method that the Splunk platform uses to extract LDAP credentials from client certificates. This setting takes one of the following values: CommonName... EDIPI (Electronic Data Interchange Personal Identifier)... PIV (Personal Identity Verification), a 16-digit numeric identifier typically formatted as xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx@mil. It is extracted from an 'Other Name' field in the Subject Alternate Name which corresponds to one of the object identifiers (OIDs) that you configure in 'certBasedUserAuthPivOidList'. No default." CAC page: accepted values CommonName, EDIPI or PIV; without it "LDAP certificate extraction won't happen".

web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthPiv.correction: Drop the condition; the vendor default is non-empty. If the objective is DoD-specific OIDs, test for them by value rather than for non-emptiness.
web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthPiv.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: certBasedUserAuthPivOidList = 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.3, Microsoft Universal Principal Name, Microsoft User Principal Name, from etc/system/default/web.conf - three entries, non-empty.
web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthPiv.notes: The condition is 'non_empty' and the vendor ships a three-entry default, so it is satisfied out of the box and never appears in any observed_reason - SRG-APP-000154-AU-002360 is Open on requireClientCert, enableCertBasedUserAuth and certBasedUserAuthMethod, not on this. The rationale ("an empty list leaves PIV extraction with nothing to query") describes a state the product does not ship in. Incidental: the vendor CAC page lists only two of the three default entries, so the published default and the shipped default disagree.
web.conf\tsettings\tcertBasedUserAuthPiv.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "A list of object identifiers (OIDs) that the Splunk platform uses to lookup an end-user's PIV info in the Subject Alternate Name extension of the client certificate... Default: 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.3, Microsoft Universal Principal Name, Microsoft User Principal Name". The CAC page gives the default as "1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.3, Microsoft Universal Principal Name" and says multiple OIDs are comma-separated.

web.conf\tsettings\tcipherSuite.correction: web.conf [settings] cipherSuite matches ^((ECDHE|DHE)-(ECDSA|RSA)-AES(128|256)-(GCM-)?SHA(256|384))(:((ECDHE|DHE)-(ECDSA|RSA)-AES(128|256)-(GCM-)?SHA(256|384)))*$ , and move the TLS 1.3 suite list to a server.conf [tls1.3] cipherSuite condition.
web.conf\tsettings\tcipherSuite.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: the shipped default is eight ECDHE suites (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 through ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256); 'splunk cmd openssl ciphers -v' resolves all eight as TLSv1.2. Operand test against the instance's OpenSSL 3.5.7 as a cipher_list: 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384' returns 'Error in cipher list ... SSL_CTX_set_cipher_list:no cipher match', and so does 'AES128-CCM-SHA256'; 'AES256-GCM-SHA384' resolves but is a static-RSA suite with no forward secrecy. The live TLS 1.3 handshake negotiates TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 although no TLS_* name appears anywhere in cipherSuite, which demonstrates that the TLS 1.3 suite is selected outside this setting.
web.conf\tsettings\tcipherSuite.notes: The regex admits three classes of value the setting cannot carry or should not carry: TLS 1.3 names such as TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, which the instance's OpenSSL rejects outright as a cipher_list and which the vendor documents as belonging only to server.conf [tls1.3]; AES128-CCM-SHA256, which is not a cipher name in this build at all; and bare AES256-GCM-SHA384, a suite with no forward secrecy. The three non_empty conditions are sound and already pass. A second, structural point: because web.conf cipherSuite governs TLS 1.2 only and TLS 1.3 is on by default in 10.4.2, no cipherSuite condition can fully discharge SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000151 or WSR-000188 - the TLS 1.3 half needs a server.conf [tls1.3] condition.
web.conf\tsettings\tcipherSuite.vendor_says: Vendor page: "The cipherSuite setting controls TLS 1.2 cipher suites." TLS 1.3 suites are configured in the [tls1.3] stanza of server.conf, whose own cipherSuite key "accepts only TLS 1.3 cipher suite names and does not accept TLS 1.2 cipher suite names". The 10.4.2 spec: "If set, uses the specified cipher string for the HTTP server. If not set, uses the default cipher string provided by OpenSSL... The default can vary. See the cipherSuite setting in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/system/default/web.conf for the current default."

web.conf\tsettings\tcookieSameSite.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: cookieSameSite = lax from etc/system/default/web.conf (line 551). Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tcookieSameSite.notes: A clean example of the stale-spec effect. Under the 10.0.0 default (not_specified) the condition 'in lax|strict' would be a genuine gap; under 10.4.2 the vendor ships lax and the condition is satisfied out of the box. The operand tokens are drawn correctly from the documented four-value vocabulary. Keep the condition as a guard against a site setting 'none' for dashboard embedding, which the vendor documents as requiring x_frame_options_sameorigin = false as well - a pair worth noting together.
web.conf\tsettings\tcookieSameSite.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "cookieSameSite = [ not_specified | lax | strict | none ]... A value of 'lax' means the Splunk web server sets the 'SameSite=Lax' attribute. A value of 'strict' means... 'SameSite=Strict'. A value of 'none' means... to let browsers send the cookies in all contexts... The 'SameSite=None' attribute in a cookie requires that you set the 'Secure' attribute... Default: lax". The 10.0.0 spec states "Default: not_specified".

web.conf\tsettings\tecdhCurves.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: ecdhCurves = prime256v1, secp384r1, secp521r1 from the shipped default, which satisfies both conditions as written. 'splunk cmd openssl ecparam -list_curves' - the command the spec itself directs you to run - lists all three short names, so the operand is valid for this build.
web.conf\tsettings\tecdhCurves.notes: Both conditions (non_empty, and the exact three-curve regex) are already satisfied by the vendor default, and neither appears in any observed_reason, so they contribute nothing to the Open verdicts. The operand is valid against the instance's own curve list. One caveat worth carrying: the rationale asserts "the server supports only the curves specified in the list", which the vendor scopes to TLS 1.2 - TLS 1.3 key exchange groups come from server.conf [tls1.3] groups, so on a 10.4.2 listener this criterion no longer governs the key exchange the live handshake actually used.
web.conf\tsettings\tecdhCurves.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "A list of ECDH curves to use for ECDH key negotiation... The server supports only the curves specified in the list. Splunk software only supports named curves that have been specified by their SHORT names... Example setting: 'ecdhCurves = prime256v1,secp384r1,secp521r1'. The default can vary." Vendor page: the [sslConfig] setting "controls key exchange curves for TLS 1.2 connections", and for TLS 1.3 "the equivalent setting is 'groups' in the [tls1.3] stanza".

web.conf\tsettings\tenableCertBasedUserA.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; absent from the shipped default web.conf, so false is in effect. Operand acceptance untested for the same expired-session reason given under requireClientCert.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableCertBasedUserA.notes: The setting, stanza and default are all as the criteria state, so the findings are genuine. Three dependencies the criteria do not carry, all vendor-documented and all consequential. The CAC page requires SSOMode = permissive and trustedIP = 127.0.0.1, which makes these seven conditions mutually unsatisfiable with the SSOMode condition under SRG-APP-000223-WSR-000145. LDAP is mandatory, so this cannot be met on a native-authentication instance - that is an external dependency. And the spec warns that turning it on disables splunkd's own check that Splunk Web is serving requests, which is an availability consequence the fix text should state. Same 'equals true' versus 'in true|True|TRUE|t|1|yes' inconsistency as requireClientCert, across four and three ids respectively.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableCertBasedUserA.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "Whether or not user authentication with certificates is enabled... When this setting has a value of 'true', 'requireClientCert' must *also* have a value of 'true'. NOTE: Splunkd disables the check to determine if Splunk Web is serving web requests after it completes startup when this setting has a value of 'true'. If you need this check to happen, then this setting *must* have a value of 'false'. Default: false". CAC page: default false, set to true, "a requirement for CAC-based authentication"; applies to "Splunk Enterprise version 9.0.2 and higher only"; LDAP is required and "No other scheme type, including native authentication, works for this purpose."

web.conf\tsettings\tenableSplunkWebSSL.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: enableSplunkWebSSL = true, sourced from etc/system/local/web.conf. Verified in practice: the listener on port 8000 completes a TLS handshake (TLSv1.2 with ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, TLSv1.3 with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), so HTTPS is genuinely in effect rather than merely configured.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableSplunkWebSSL.notes: The most-used setting in the file and the criteria are correct: the default is false, the fix is to set it, and nothing here is misstated. It never appears in an observed_reason because this instance sets it in system/local. One consistency defect across the twelve ids: four different operand forms are in use - 'equals true', 'in 1|true', 'in true|1' and 'matches ^(1|true)$'. 'equals true' alone rejects the value 1, which the product STIG fix text itself writes (enableSplunkWebSSL = 1), so an instance built to the fix text would fail three ids and pass the other nine. Standardize on 'in 1|true'.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableSplunkWebSSL.vendor_says: "Toggle between http or https. Set to true to enable https and SSL. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tenableWebDebug.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: enableWebDebug = False from etc/system/default/web.conf. The condition appears in no observed_reason, so it was scored as passing.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableWebDebug.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default and correctly scored, so it does not contribute to SRG-APP-000266-WSR-000160 (which is Open on request.show_tracebacks and simple_xml_perf_debug). The condition is well chosen for "debugging and trace information must be disabled" and is worth keeping as a guard. 'not_equals true' resolves correctly against the capitalized shipped value under the assessment's comparison.
web.conf\tsettings\tenableWebDebug.vendor_says: "Whether or not the debug REST endpoints are accessible, for example., /debug/**splat. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tenable_insecure_logi.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: enable_insecure_login = False from etc/system/default/web.conf (line 223). Appears in no observed_reason, so the assessment scored it as passing.
web.conf\tsettings\tenable_insecure_logi.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, so it contributes nothing to SRG-APP-000178-AU-002660, which is Open on two limits.conf conditions. The condition and its rationale are both accurate - the vendor's own example URL shows the password as a query parameter - so it is a good guard to keep. The setting is correctly placed in web.conf [settings].
web.conf\tsettings\tenable_insecure_logi.vendor_says: "Whether or not the GET-based '/account/insecurelogin' REST endpoint is enabled. Provides an alternate GET-based authentication mechanism. If 'true', the following url is available: http://localhost:8000/en-US/account/insecurelogin?loginType=splunk&username=noc&password=XXXXXXX. If 'false', only the main /account/login endpoint is available. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tengine.autoreload.on.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: engine.autoreload.on = False from etc/system/default/web.conf. Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tengine.autoreload.on.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, so it contributes nothing to the Open verdict. Reasonable as a guard against a development facility being left on, though note the setting is an availability control as much as a debugging one - an auto-restarting appserver is a stability concern, not an information-disclosure one, so the rationale's framing is a little loose.
web.conf\tsettings\tengine.autoreload.on.vendor_says: "Whether or not the appserver will auto-restart if it detects a python file has changed. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tforceHttp10.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: forceHttp10 = auto from etc/system/default/web.conf. Appears in no observed_reason, so it was scored as passing.
web.conf\tsettings\tforceHttp10.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, and the operand is correctly drawn from the documented three-value vocabulary, so the condition is well formed. It does not drive SRG-APP-000251-WSR-000194, which rests solely on the max_upload_size condition and is false. Two observations on fit: the spec text for this setting describes "the REST HTTP server", which reads as carried over from server.conf, and excluding only 'never' permits 'always' - a value the vendor documents as withholding HTTP/1.1 features, which is a compatibility choice rather than a normalization control. The requirement's real subject, interpreting and normalizing ambiguous requests, is not something web.conf exposes a setting for.
web.conf\tsettings\tforceHttp10.vendor_says: "forceHttp10 = auto|never|always. How the HTTP server deals with HTTP/1.0 support for incoming clients. When set to 'always', the REST HTTP server does not use some HTTP 1.1 features such as persistent connections or chunked transfer encoding. When set to 'auto', it limits HTTP 1.1 features only if the client sent no User-Agent header, or if the user agent is known to have bugs in its HTTP/1.1 support. When set to 'never', it always allows HTTP 1.1, even to clients it suspects might be buggy. Default: auto"

web.conf\tsettings\thttpport.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: httpport = 8000 from etc/system/default/web.conf, and the port is confirmed listening (0.0.0.0:8000, socket owned by splunkd pid 2206). Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\thttpport.notes: The vendor ships a value and the listener is up, so 'present' is satisfied and the condition contributes nothing to SRG-APP-000142-WSR-000089 - which is Open on server.socket_host and SPLUNK_BINDIP, both genuine. The condition is correct for the port half of "a specified IP address and port" and worth keeping, though a bare 'present' test will always pass on a running instance since the spec says Splunk Web cannot start without it.
web.conf\tsettings\thttpport.vendor_says: "httpport = <positive integer>. The TCP port on which Splunk Web listens for incoming connections. Must be present for Splunk Web to start. If omitted or 0 the server will NOT start an http listener. If using SSL, set to the HTTPS port number. Default: 8000"

web.conf\tsettings\tjs_logger_mode.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: js_logger_mode = None from etc/system/default/web.conf; related keys js_logger_mode_server_end_point = util/log/js and js_logger_mode_server_max_buffer = 100 are also present. Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tjs_logger_mode.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default. The operand tokens are quoted exactly from the spec's three-value vocabulary, so 'not_in Firebug|Server' is correctly formed and leaves only the compliant value None. Good condition, no change needed; it simply does not drive the finding.
web.conf\tsettings\tjs_logger_mode.vendor_says: "js_logger_mode = [None | Firebug | Server]. The JavaScript Logger mode. Available modes: None, Firebug, Server. Mode None: Does not log anything. Mode Firebug: Use firebug by default if it exists, or defer to the older less promiscuous version of firebug lite. Mode Server: Log to a defined server endpoint... Default: None"

web.conf\tsettings\tlog.access_file.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: log.access_file = web_access.log from etc/system/default/web.conf. Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tlog.access_file.notes: The vendor ships a filename, so 'non_empty' is satisfied and the condition contributes nothing to the three findings - all of which are Open on props.conf or savedsearches.conf conditions instead. The condition is sound as a prerequisite (the record whose timestamp or alerting is assessed must exist and be named), and it is correctly placed. Note that the timestamp format and time zone objectives behind SRG-APP-000374 and SRG-APP-000375 are properties of how the file is parsed, which is props.conf territory, not web.conf - so this file's share of those requirements really is only that the log exists.
web.conf\tsettings\tlog.access_file.vendor_says: "log.access_file = <filename>. The HTTP access log filename. This file is written in the default $SPLUNK_HOME/var/log directory. Default: web_access.log" Related shipped settings: log.access_maxsize = 25000000 and log.access_maxfiles = 5.

web.conf\tsettings\tlogin_content.notes: The setting, stanza and absence of a default are all correct, the operands are satisfiable - a substring match works on the single line the vendor requires - and the finding is genuine, confirmed by fetching the live login page. The defect is only in SRG-APP-000069-AU-000420: that requirement asks that the banner be retained on screen "until users acknowledge the usage conditions", and the vendor documents no acknowledgement mechanism for the login page. login_content is informational text only. The display half of the objective is the application's share; the acknowledgement half is not configurable and must not be carried as a condition. Two practical constraints for the fix text: the banner must be a single line in the file, and the platform strips HTML tags it considers dangerous.
web.conf\tsettings\tlogin_content.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "Lets you add custom content to the login page. Supports any text including HTML. The Splunk platform sanitizes HTML for security purposes by removing potentially dangerous tags and attributes. No default." web.conf\tsettings\tmaxSockets.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: maxSockets = 0 from etc/system/default/web.conf. btool check exits 0 with no complaint about the value.

The 'present' condition under SRG-APP-000142-WSR-000089 can stand.
web.conf\tsettings\tmgmtHostPort.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: mgmtHostPort = 127.0.0.1:8089 from etc/system/default/web.conf - not the 0.0.0.0:8089 the vendor documents as the default. Neither condition appears in any observed_reason - the regex passes on this instance because the shipped default happens to be 127.0.0.1:8089 - so no finding is currently misreported, but the criterion would pass an instance whose management port is fully exposed, and would fail an instance configured exactly as the vendor documents the default.
web.conf\tsettings\tmgmtHostPort.vendor_says: "The host port of the splunkd process. The IP address and host port where Splunk Web looks for the splunkd process. Default (on all other Splunk platform instance types): 0.0.0.0:8089" The Bind Splunk to an IP page adds that if SPLUNK_BINDIP is changed you "must also change mgmtHostPort to use the same IP address".

web.conf\tsettings\tpid_path.correction: Drop the condition and move the objective to external_dependencies: ownership and mode of $SPLUNK_HOME/var/run/splunk and of splunkd.pid, and the service manager's restriction on who may stop the splunkd unit.
web.conf\tsettings\tpid_path.live_evidence: The line is present but commented out in the shipped etc/system/default/web.conf (line 428: '# pid_path = var/run/splunk/splunkweb.pid'), so btool reports no value. web.conf\tsettings\tpid_path.notes: This is the only failing condition recorded for SRG-APP-000435-WSR-000147. Three things are wrong. The vendor tells the operator not to set it. The file it names is not produced in 10.4.2, because Splunk Web is not a separately stoppable process - the pid that matters is splunkd.pid. And naming a pid file does not protect a process from being stopped; that is filesystem permission and service-manager policy, which is outside what the application configures. There is no web.conf setting that discharges this requirement.
web.conf\tsettings\tpid_path.vendor_says: "Specifies the path to the Process IDentification (pid) number file. Must be set to 'var/run/splunk/splunkweb.pid'. CAUTION: Do not change this parameter." The spec states no default.

web.conf\tsettings\tremoteUserMatchExact.correction: Require web.conf [settings] remoteUserMatchExact equals 1 only where header-based SSO is in use (server.conf [general] trustedIP non_empty). web.conf\tsettings\tremoteUserMatchExact.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: remoteUserMatchExact = 0 from etc/system/default/web.conf. This is the sole failing condition behind SRG-APP-000223-WSR-000145.

It has no bearing at all on an instance that does not use header-based SSO - and this instance does not, since trustedIP is unset and SSOMode is strict. When set to 0, dashes and underscores are not considered to be distinct, to retain compatibility with older versions of Splunk software. Set to 1 when you set up SSO. Default: 0"

web.conf\tsettings\trequireClientCert.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; not present in btool web list --debug because it is absent from the shipped default web.conf, so the compiled-in default false is in effect. The test I would run is a POST of requireClientCert=yes to /servicesNS/nobody/search/configs/conf-zz_probe_web followed by a btool read-back and a DELETE.
web.conf\tsettings\trequireClientCert.notes: Right setting, right stanza, right default, and the vendor CAC page confirms it must be true for card authentication - the findings are genuine. One inconsistency to fix: four SRG ids use 'equals true' and four use 'in true|True|TRUE|t|1|yes' for the same setting, so one instance can be judged both compliant and non-compliant depending on which id is being scored. Only 'true' is documented; the wider list is unverified and should be narrowed to 'in true|1' or made uniform across all eight. Note also that the mechanism this setting gates depends on DoD PKI issuance and an LDAP directory, which belong in external_dependencies.
web.conf\tsettings\trequireClientCert.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "Whether or not an HTTPS client that connects to the Splunk Web HTTPS server must present a certificate that was signed by the same certificate authority (CA) that signed the certificate that was installed on this instance... If you give 'enableCertBasedUserAuth' a value of 'true', then the previous statements do not apply. Instead, the instance uses the root CA certificate defined in the 'sslRootCAPath' setting in web.conf... Default: false". The CAC page lists it in web.conf, default false, and calls it "a requirement for CAC-based authentication".

web.conf\tsettings\tserver.socket_host.live_evidence: Not set; listenOnIPv6 = no, so the effective value is 0.0.0.0. Confirmed at the socket layer: /proc/net/tcp shows 00000000:1F40 (0.0.0.0:8000) LISTEN, and the socket inode is held by pid 2206, splunkd. The Python appserver (pid 2474) holds 127.0.0.1:8065 only, consistent with the spec's statement that appServerPorts "is bound only on the loopback interface -- it is not exposed to the network at large". Whether writing a specific address into server.socket_host rebinds splunkd's 8000 socket could not be tested, because that requires a restart.
web.conf\tsettings\tserver.socket_host.notes: The finding is genuine in substance: the setting is unset, the documented default is any-interface, and the listener is measurably on 0.0.0.0. The operand names exactly the two any-address values the spec defines, so it is correct. Two caveats for the write-up. First, the externally reachable port 8000 is splunkd's socket, not the Python appserver's, so the vendor's attribution of this setting to "the Splunk Web process (splunkweb)" is looser than it reads in 10.4.2; the effect of an override is untested here. Second, the assessor's own observed_reason already pairs this with splunk-launch.conf SPLUNK_BINDIP, which the vendor documents as covering port 8000 - keeping both conditions is right, and the vendor also warns that if SPLUNK_BINDIP is changed, mgmtHostPort must be changed to match.
web.conf\tsettings\tserver.socket_host.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "Host values may be any IPv4 or IPv6 address, or any valid hostname. The string 'localhost' is a synonym for '127.0.0.1'... The string '0.0.0.0' is a special IPv4 entry meaning 'any active interface' (INADDR_ANY), and '::' is the similar IN6ADDR_ANY for IPv6. Default (if 'listenOnIPV6' is set to \"no\"): 0.0.0.0. Default (otherwise): '::'". Bind Splunk to an IP: "To bind the Splunk Web process (splunkweb) to a specific IP, use the server.socket_host setting", and SPLUNK_BINDIP's scope is listed as including "Splunk Web port 8000 (by default)".

A certificate path can satisfy 'matches tls1\.2' only if the file name happens to contain the literal string tls1.2, so the condition is unmeetable in practice and is what records this finding Open; the three not_matches conditions pass vacuously against any path and test nothing at all. The other serverCert conditions (non_empty for five SRG ids, not_equals the shipped default path for SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000151) are sound and already pass on this instance.
web.conf\tsettings\tserverCert.vendor_says: "Full path to the Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) format Splunk web server certificate file. The file may also contain root and intermediate certificates, if required... Default: $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/splunkweb/cert.pem". It is a filesystem path, not a protocol list.

web.conf\tsettings\tsimple_error_page.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: simple_error_page = False from the shipped default. The spec notes the verbose page also carries "crashes" and "debug output", which were not exercised here.

If set to 'true', Splunk Web displays a simplified error page for errors (404, 500, etc.) that only contain the error status. If set to 'false', Splunk Web displays a more verbose error page that contains the home link, message, a more_results_link, crashes, referrer, debug output, and byline. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\tsslRootCAPath.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; not set on this instance, so the server.conf fallback applies.
web.conf\tsettings\tsslRootCAPath.notes: Right setting for "only accept client certificates issued by DoD PKI or DoD-approved CAs", and the finding is genuine. One refinement worth recording: because the spec documents a fallback to server.conf's sslRootCAPath, an instance that sets only the server.conf value is still correctly configured, so a strict web.conf non_empty condition can report a gap that does not exist. The condition should accept either location.
web.conf\tsettings\tsslRootCAPath.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "The path to a root certificate authority (CA) certificate, in privacy-enhanced mail (PEM) format, that splunkd is to use to authenticate client certificates under certain specific conditions. If this setting has no value, splunkd falls back to the value of the 'sslRootCAPath' setting in server.conf... No default." web.conf\tsettings\tsslVersions.correction: web.conf [settings] sslVersions not_matches (^|,)\s*(ssl3|tls1\.0|tls1\.1|\*|tls)\s*(,|$)  AND  web.conf [settings] sslVersions matches (^|,)\s*tls1\.(2|3)\s*(,|$)
web.conf\tsettings\tsslVersions.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: sslVersions = tls1.2, tls1.3 from etc/system/default/web.conf. Protocol probe against the live listener with the instance's own OpenSSL 3.5.7 (splunk cmd openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8000): -tls1 and -tls1_1 both return 'tlsv1 alert protocol version' (SSL alert 70, rejected); -tls1_2 negotiates TLSv1.2 with ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384; -tls1_3 negotiates TLSv1.3 with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.
web.conf\tsettings\tsslVersions.notes: Two separate defects, both from the 10.0.0 vocabulary. (1) The regex ^\s*(tls1\.2|\*|tls)(\s*,\s*-(ssl2|ssl3|tls1\.0|tls1\.1))*\s*$ has no tls1.3 token, so it cannot be satisfied by the 10.4.2 vendor default and drives the Open verdicts on SRG-APP-000014-WSR-000006 and SRG-APP-000015-WSR-000014 against a listener that measurably refuses TLS 1.0 and 1.1. (2) 'equals tls1.2' drives SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000151 and SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000156; satisfying it removes TLS 1.3 from a requirement that asks for encryption strength, so the criterion inverts its own objective. SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000156's observed_reason shows the same 'equals tls1.2' criterion failing identically across web.conf, server.conf, inputs.conf, outputs.conf and alert_actions.conf - the whole finding is an artifact of the stale operand. The remaining sslVersions criteria (matches tls1\.2, not_matches ssl3/tls1.0/tls1.1, not_in *|tls) are sound and already pass.
web.conf\tsettings\tsslVersions.vendor_says: The 10.4.2 spec: "The versions available are 'tls1.0', 'tls1.1', 'tls1.2' and 'tls1.3'" and "SSL versions 2 and 3 are always disabled." The vendor TLS page: TLS 1.3 is supported from Splunk Enterprise 10.4.0 and is enabled by default alongside TLS 1.2 on new installs and upgrades; "Turn on TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 (the default in version 10.4.0)"; TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are off by default in 10.4.0 and higher; sslVersions=tls1.3 selects TLS 1.3 only; sslVersions=-tls1.3 reverts to TLS 1.2 only.

web.conf\tsettings\tstartwebserver.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: startwebserver = 1, sourced from etc/system/local/web.conf on this instance (the shipped default is also 1). Appears in no observed_reason.

web.conf\tsettings\tstartwebserver.vendor_says: "startwebserver = [0 | 1]. Set whether or not to start Splunk Web. 0 disables Splunk Web, 1 enables it. Default: 1"
