The requirement's data-entry half is carried by tools.decode.on; this one is the response side.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.encode.on.vendor_says: "Whether or not to encode all controller method response strings into UTF-8 str objects in Python. CAUTION: Disabling this will likely cause high byte character encoding to fail. Default: true"

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.base.correction: Same as tools.proxy.on: assert web.conf [settings] tools.proxy.base non_empty only where tools.proxy.on is true, and note that the spec requires the value to carry a scheme as well as host and port (<scheme>://<URL>), which a bare non_empty test does not check.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.base.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; absent from the shipped default web.conf and from btool output, consistent with the documented empty-string default.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.base.notes: The dependency the criterion's rationale quotes is real and correctly quoted - setting tools.proxy.on without tools.proxy.base is a misconfiguration. But the condition inherits the applicability defect: it is only meaningful once a proxy exists. Secondary operand point, 'non_empty' admits any string, while the vendor documents a specific shape (<scheme>://<URL> with host name and network port), so a value that cannot work would still satisfy the condition.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.base.vendor_says: "tools.proxy.base = <scheme>://<URL>. The proxy base URL in Splunk Web. Default: empty string" The tools.proxy.on entry adds: "If you set this to 'true', you must also set 'tools.proxy.base' to a valid host name and network port."

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.on.correction: Make the pair conditional on a proxy actually being deployed - assert tools.proxy.on equals true and tools.proxy.base non_empty only where the architecture places a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of Splunk Web - and record the presence or absence of that proxy in external_dependencies.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.on.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; absent from the shipped default web.conf and from btool output, so false is in effect. With tools.proxy.base it forms the only two failing conditions behind SRG-APP-000098-WSR-000060.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.on.notes: The requirement is itself conditional: "A web server, behind a load balancer or proxy server, must produce log records containing the client IP information." Asserting tools.proxy.on = true unconditionally inverts the vendor's guidance for a direct-access deployment, because it makes the instance trust X-Forwarded-* and X-Url-Scheme headers supplied by the immediate client - which on a directly reachable listener is a client-controlled-input problem, not a hardening measure. Since these two conditions are the only failures behind SRG-APP-000098-WSR-000060, the finding as written says that an instance with no proxy is non-compliant for not pretending to have one. Whether a proxy exists is an architecture fact outside web.conf.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.proxy.on.vendor_says: "Whether or not the Splunk platform instance is behind a reverse proxy server. If set to 'true', the instance assumes that it is behind a reverse proxy and uses HTTP header information from the proxy to log access requests, secure its cookies properly, and generate valid URLs for redirect responses. All of the instance's HTTP services will use information from 'X-Forwarded-*', 'Front-End-Https', and 'X-Url-Scheme' headers, where available, to override what it receives from proxied requests. If you set this to 'true', you must also set 'tools.proxy.base' to a valid host name and network port. If set to 'false', the instance relies on its own internal HTTP server settings and the immediate client's HTTP headers... Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.force.correction: Gate it on the proxy being in use: require web.conf [settings] tools.sessions.forceSecure in 1|true only where web.conf [settings] tools.proxy.on equals true. Where Splunk Web terminates TLS itself, enableSplunkWebSSL in 1|true together with tools.sessions.secure in 1|true discharges the objective.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.force.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: tools.sessions.forceSecure = False from etc/system/default/web.conf, and the condition is recorded as failing for both ids. The same instance serves HTTPS directly (enableSplunkWebSSL = true, TLS handshake confirmed on port 8000) with tools.sessions.secure = True, and tools.proxy.on is unset, so the one case this setting addresses does not arise here.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.force.notes: The vendor scopes this setting to exactly one topology: a proxy terminating HTTPS with an HTTP back-end hop. On an instance that serves HTTPS directly and has tools.sessions.secure true, the Secure attribute is already set, so the condition reports a gap that is not there - and it is one of only two failing conditions behind SRG-APP-000439-WSR-000152 and WSR-000155 in web.conf. Setting it true is harmless, so this is a precision defect rather than a harmful one, but as written it will record an Open finding on a correctly configured direct-TLS deployment.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.force.vendor_says: "Whether or not the secure bit of a session cookie that has been sent over HTTPS is set. If a client connects to a proxy server over HTTPS, and the back end connects to Splunk over HTTP, then setting this to 'true' forces the session cookie being sent back to the client over HTTPS to have the secure bit set. Default: false"

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.on.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: tools.sessions.on = True from etc/system/default/web.conf. Recorded in no observed_reason, so the assessment scored it as passing.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.on.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default, which the spec also instructs never be changed, so the condition cannot drive either finding. SRG-APP-000223-WSR-000145 is Open on remoteUserMatchExact alone. The condition is reasonable to keep as a guard against someone disabling session support.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.on.vendor_says: The spec states the setting as a literal rather than a type: "tools.sessions.on = true. Whether or not user session support is enabled. Always set this to true." No default is stated.

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.resta.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: tools.sessions.restart_persist = True from etc/system/default/web.conf (capitalized in the vendor's own default file). Both conditions are recorded as failing in the assessment's observed_reason, which confirms its comparison is case-insensitive and that the capitalized default does not create a false pass.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.resta.notes: Setting, stanza, default and semantics all check out, and the finding is genuine: the vendor ships true, which keeps the session cookie across browser restarts. Both operand forms in use ('not_equals true' under SRG-APP-000220-WSR-000201 and 'equals false' under SRG-APP-000389-AU-000180) resolve correctly here. 'equals false' is the stronger of the two and is preferable for both ids, since 'not_equals true' would also be satisfied by an unrecognized value. The criterion's own rationale under SRG-APP-000220-WSR-000201 wrongly says "the vendor default already declines to do so" - the default is true, which is the opposite; the condition is right but the stated reason is not.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.resta.vendor_says: "Whether or not the session cookie is deleted from the browser when the browser quits. If set to 'false', then the session cookie is deleted from the browser upon the browser quitting. If set to 'true', then sessions persist across browser restarts, assuming the 'tools.sessions.timeout' has not been reached. Default: true"

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.secur.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: tools.sessions.secure = True from etc/system/default/web.conf. The condition appears in no observed_reason, so the assessment scored it as passing - confirming its comparison tolerates the vendor's capitalized boolean.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.secur.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default and correctly scored as such, so it contributes nothing to the three Open verdicts. Keeping the condition is harmless and documents the dependency on enableSplunkWebSSL. Worth stating in the write-up that this setting plus enableSplunkWebSSL is what actually discharges "session IDs must be sent using SSL/TLS" - which matters for the tools.sessions.forceSecure verdict below.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.secur.vendor_says: "Whether or not the browser must transmit session cookies over an HTTPS connection when Splunk Web is configured to serve requests using HTTPS (the 'enableSplunkWebSSL' setting is 'true'.) If set to 'true' and 'enableSplunkWebSSL' is also 'true', then the browser must transmit the session cookie over HTTPS connections. This improves session security. Default: true"

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.timeo.correction: Keep web.conf [settings] tools.sessions.timeout present and min 2. Replace the independent 15-minute bounds with a pair whose sum holds: web.conf [settings] tools.sessions.timeout max 5 together with web.conf [settings] ui_inactivity_timeout max 10 (any split summing to 15 or less), and add a server.conf [general] sessionTimeout condition so the smaller-of-the-two rule cannot raise the result.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.timeo.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: tools.sessions.timeout = 60 from etc/system/default/web.conf, so 'present' and 'min 2' pass and 'max 15' fails - which is what records these four findings Open.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.timeo.notes: 'max 15' is faithful to the product STIG check text and the finding is genuine against a default of 60, so the direction is right. What the criterion gets wrong is the arithmetic: the vendor documents the effective inactivity window as ui_inactivity_timeout plus the smaller of the splunkweb and splunkd timeouts. Bounding each key at 15 independently therefore permits a 30-minute window, which does not meet the 15-minute reauthentication objective behind SRG-APP-000295-AU-000190, SRG-APP-000295-WSR-000134 or SRG-APP-000389-AU-000180. It is sufficient for SRG-APP-000295-WSR-000012, whose ceiling is eight hours. The 'min 2' condition is quoted verbatim from the spec and is sound. Also note that a change here needs a restart to take effect, which the fix text should say.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.sessions.timeo.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "The number of minutes of inactivity before a user session is expired. The countdown for this setting effectively resets every minute through browser activity until the 'ui_inactivity_timeout' setting is reached. Use a value of 2 or higher, as a value of 1 causes a race condition with the browser refresh, producing unpredictable behavior. Low values are not useful except for testing. Default: 60". Vendor admin page: the splunkweb/splunkd countdown "does not begin until the browser session reaches its timeout value", and to get the total you "add the value of ui_inactivity_timeout to the smaller of the timeout values for splunkweb and splunkd" - worked example "The user session stays active for 25 minutes (15m+10m)". When web.conf and server.conf sessionTimeout are both set, "the smaller of the two timeout attributes prevails".

web.conf\tsettings\ttools.staticdir.gene.correction: Write it so absence satisfies it: web.conf [settings] tools.staticdir.generate_indexes absent_or_in 0 (and drop 'false', which is not in the documented [1 | 0] vocabulary).
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.staticdir.gene.live_evidence: Documented in the 10.4.2 shipped spec under [settings]; absent from the shipped default web.conf and from btool output, so the documented default of 0 is in effect. The assessment records it as failing ('not set') for all three ids.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.staticdir.gene.notes: This is the decisive one of the absence-is-failure defects, because it is the only failing condition recorded for SRG-APP-000141-WSR-000083 ("web.conf [settings] tools.staticdir.generate_indexes in 0|false -> not set") and for SRG-APP-000266-WSR-000142 (same key, 'not_equals 1'), so both findings are false in their entirety. It is also one of the three spurious components of SRG-APP-000141-WSR-000087. The criterion's own rationale states the default is 0, which is the compliant value - absence cannot be a finding. Secondary nit: the documented vocabulary is [1 | 0], so the token 'false' in 'in 0|false' is undocumented, though harmless.
web.conf\tsettings\ttools.staticdir.gene.vendor_says: "tools.staticdir.generate_indexes = [1 | 0]. Whether or not the webserver serves a directory listing for static directories. Default: 0 (false)"

web.conf\tsettings\tui_inactivity_timeou.correction: web.conf [settings] ui_inactivity_timeout min 1 AND max 10, paired with tools.sessions.timeout max 5, so that the documented sum is 15 or less.
web.conf\tsettings\tui_inactivity_timeou.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: ui_inactivity_timeout = 60 from etc/system/default/web.conf. 'min 1' passes; 'max 15' fails, and it is one of the conditions recording SRG-APP-000389-AU-000180 Open.
web.conf\tsettings\tui_inactivity_timeou.notes: 'min 1' is quoted straight from the spec and is sound. 'max 15' is the other half of the additive error described under tools.sessions.timeout: 15 here plus 15 there is a 30-minute inactivity window, not 15. The rationale under SRG-APP-000389-AU-000180 is close to the right insight - it says a value above the session timeout "lets client-side polling extend the effective inactivity window past it" - but the operand it chose does not implement that insight. Note also that 'min 1' is only correctly applied to SRG-APP-000295-AU-000190 and SRG-APP-000295-WSR-000134 as a guard; neither is Open on it.
web.conf\tsettings\tui_inactivity_timeou.vendor_says: 10.4.2 spec: "The length of time lapsed, in minutes, for notification when there is no user interface clicking, mouseover, scrolling, or resizing. Notifies client side pollers to stop, resulting in sessions expiring at the 'tools.sessions.timeout' value. If less than 1, results in no timeout notification ever being triggered (Sessions stay alive for as long as the browser is open). Default: 60". Vendor admin page: "The Splunk browser session will time out once this value is reached. The default is 60 minutes", and "If ui_inactivity_timeout is set to less than 1, there's no timeout -- the session will stay alive while the browser is open."

web.conf\tsettings\tx_frame_options_same.live_evidence: btool web list --debug: x_frame_options_sameorigin = True from etc/system/default/web.conf (line 98). Appears in no observed_reason.
web.conf\tsettings\tx_frame_options_same.notes: Already satisfied by the vendor default. Worth keeping as a guard precisely because the vendor documents one legitimate reason to turn it off - embedding dashboards in a third-party iframe - so a site that has done that will show up. The rationale's framing of SAMEORIGIN as "a means for the client to establish application authenticity" is a stretch; the header prevents framing, which is a clickjacking control rather than an authenticity one, but the setting choice itself is right.
web.conf\tsettings\tx_frame_options_same.vendor_says: "adds a X-Frame-Options header set to 'SAMEORIGIN' to every response served by cherrypy. Default: true". The cookieSameSite entry adds that to embed a dashboard in a third-party iframe "You must also give the 'x_frame_options_sameorigin' setting a value of 'false'".
